This paper examines Uzbekistan's transition from Cyrillic to Latin script, mandated in 1993 and implemented in schools from 1996. I study heterogeneous effects across initial conditions using a difference\u2010in\u2010differences design that exploits variation in exposure across birth cohorts and pre\u2010reform district characteristics. The reform had no significant average effect on literacy, but it generated substantial heterogeneity: districts with lower baseline literacy gained 0.09 standard deviations per standard deviation of the baseline literacy gap, whereas districts with more Russian speakers experienced relative losses of about 0.05 standard deviations. These patterns reveal the redistributive politics of nation\u2010building. The reform also reshaped labour markets: Latin\u2010exposed cohorts moved away from state employment and, less sharply, from entrepreneurship. The same cohorts became more likely to express intolerance towards speakers of other languages, an effect specific to the linguistic margin. The findings suggest that script reforms do not deliver aggregate literacy improvements but have significant distributional consequences and may heighten ethnolinguistic                   <jats:p>Quasi‐stationary band‐shaped precipitation systems (QBPSs) are the major cause of localized heavy‐rainfall events (HREs) in Japan. Using hourly radar/raingauge‐analysed precipitation amounts from 1989 to 2022, we statistically examined the occurrence characteristics of QBPSs and their associated environmental conditions. A total of 849 QBPSs were extracted during the 34‐year period, with the highest frequencies in western and southern Japan. Approximately 45% of them occurred in association with stationary fronts, and approximately 85% of them were oriented southwest–northeast or west–east. The annual occurrence frequency showed a significant increasing trend, with a regression indicating approximately a 3.4‐fold increase over the analysis period. QBPSs occurred most frequently between June and September, and their hourly frequency exhibited frequent occurrence between midnight and early morning. To elucidate the environmental characteristics favourable for QBPS formation, we analysed 225 events that occurred over Kyushu Island, western Japan, during June and July. Composite analyses using ERA5 revealed robust and coherent features: high low‐level equivalent potential temperature associated with warm and moist inflow from the East China Sea towards the Baiu frontal zone, large vertical wind shear with warm advection, synoptic‐scale ascent, low ‘level of free convection’, a deep moist layer extending into the midtroposphere, and a midlevel jet. These features were markedly pronounced relative to climatology and are consistent with previous studies on typical HREs along the Baiu frontal zone. Our results demonstrate that a combined evaluation of these environmental characteristics serves as an effective diagnostic indicator for QBPS occurrences.</jats:p>","DOI":"10.1002/qj.70333","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,15]],"date-time":"2026-10-15T23:05:02Z","timestamp":1792105502000},"update-policy":"https://doi.org/10.1002/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Characteristics of quasi‐stationary band‐shaped precipitation systems in

{"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,14]],"date-time":"2026-10-14T17:52:32Z","timestamp":1792000352622,"version":"4.4.0"},"reference-count":34,"publisher":"Public Library of Science (PLoS)","issue":"10","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,14]],"date-time":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1791936000000},"content-version":"vor","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"}],"funder":[{"DOI":"10.13039/100019395","name":"Harbor Branch Oceanographic Institute Foundation","doi-asserted-by":"publisher","award":["NA"],"award-info":[{"award-number":["NA"]}],"id":[{"id":"10.13039/100019395","id-type":"DOI","asserted-by":"publisher"}]}],"content-domain":{"domain":["www.ploswater.org"],"crossmark-restriction":false},"short-container-title":["PLOS Water"],"abstract":"<jats:p>
                    Harmful algal blooms (HABs) are increasingly impacting estuarine ecosystems, yet current microbial surveillance methods often focus on prokaryotic 16S rRNA profiles and overlook eukaryotic bloom-forming species. Here, we applied Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) MinION long-read sequencing targeting the 18S rRNA gene to characterize spatial and seasonal patterns of eukaryotic microbial communities in the Indian River Lagoon (IRL), a biologically diverse 251 km long estuary along Florida’s Atlantic coast. Water samples were collected across 20 sites during wet and dry seasons spanning subtropical and temperate subregions. Sequencing yielded high-resolution community profiles, detecting over 200 unique species and highlighting clear differences in community composition by season, region, and environmental gradients including salinity, temperature, and nutrient ratios. Eleven harmful algal bloom taxa were detected, including
                    <jats:italic>Aureoumbra lagunensis</jats:italic>
                    ,
                    <jats:italic>Karlodinium veneficum</jats:italic>
                    , and
                    <jats:italic>Pyrodinium bahamense</jats:italic>
                    , with
                    <jats:italic>A. lagunensis</jats:italic>
                    reaching >50% relative abundance in some sites. Our results show that long-read sequencing of the 18S rRNA gene can capture eukaryotic diversity and resolve potentially harmful taxa. This approach offers a promising tool for rapid, field-deployable, detection of HAB species and improves our understanding of how environmental drivers shape bloom risk across complex estuarine systems like the IRL.

title: Crossref record doi:10.1111/medu.70340: Health equity is the goal of medical education: Implications for assessment validity
text:
{"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,15]],"date-time":"2026-10-15T05:44:01Z","timestamp":1792043041878,"version":"4.4.0"},"reference-count":71,"publisher":"Wiley","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,14]],"date-time":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1791936000000},"content-version":"vor","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"},{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,14]],"date-time":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1791936000000},"content-version":"tdm","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http://doi.wiley.com/10.1002/tdm_license_1.1"}],"content-domain":{"domain":["asmepublications.onlinelibrary.wiley.com"],"crossmark-restriction":true},"short-container-title":["Medical Education"],"abstract":"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Prevailing health inequities, viewed as a matter of social justice, have catalysed an intentionality about ensuring that medical graduates can contribute to more equitable health outcomes. Medical education programmes are grappling with what this means for the assessment imperative. Attention has been given to criteria for judging assessment quality, with validity remaining an important criterion. In this paper, we explore the implications of health equity for validity and ask whether plans of assessment that do not provide evidence of students' capacity to act to advance health equity can be considered valid.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Health equity as a consideration in assessment</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We align with calls for medical education curricula and their assessment plans to fulfil medicine'ssocial contract to respond to societal health needs. We suggest that such a commitment requires us to explicitly address health equity and the inequitable health outcomes experienced by patients and communities. In turn, it challenges us to reflect on what addressing these inequities might mean for the validity and interpretation of the inferences we make from our assessments.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Reconsidering assessment validity through a health equity lens</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Drawing on scholarship related to assessment validity, health equity and social justice, we identify conceptual and practical challenges associated with foregrounding health equity as a central component of assessment validity. Using a health equity lens, we propose a set of heuristic prompts spanning purpose, constructs, evidence, inferences, learning effects, context, stakeholders, and systems and structures. These prompts are intended to foster critical reflection on how current understandings of assessment validity might be broadened when advancing health equity is recognised as a core goal of medical education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Rather than offering definitive solutions, we seek to provoke dialogue about the consequences for our students and society when we do not embrace considerations of health equity in our programmes of assessment. We contend that if medical education is committed to advancing health equity, assessment of our students cannot be deemed valid unless it provides evidence to support decisions on their ability to act towards health equity.</jats:p>

This framework captures interactions among precipitation, soil moisture, and snowpack that shape flood generation. Both simulated warming and historical records show a regional shift toward more extreme warm\u2010season, rainfall\u2010driven floods. This regional signal, however, does not translate uniformly to individual watersheds, where flood responses reflect not only warming but also the influence of subregional climate variability and sampling uncertainty. Local flood\u2010frequency changes thus remain highly uncertain despite the thermodynamic tendency toward stronger convective precipitation. Ensembles of convection\u2010permitting simulations are needed to constrain plausible local outcomes. Following maritime boundary settlements with India and Myanmar, the country gained an exclusive economic zone of 118,813 km\u00b2 and an extended continental shelf of 37,000 km\u00b2 in the Bay of Bengal, offering substantial potential in fisheries, aquaculture, renewable energy, tourism, shipping, and marine biotechnology.\nThe study synthesizes secondary data to examine the sustainable utilization of resources under the blue economy. Marine fisheries contribute 17% of national fish production, supporting millions of livelihoods, while ecosystems such as the Sundarbans and Saint Martin\u2019s Island provide vital biodiversity and climate resilience services. Yet, climate change, overfishing, habitat degradation, pollution, and fragmented governance threaten long-term sustainability, compounded by poverty and gender inequities. Opportunities exist through fisheries modernization, integrated aquaculture, renewable energy, ecosystem-based adaptation, marine biotechnology, eco-tourism, and regional cooperation.\nEffective policy interventions, including a National Ocean Policy, a dedicated Blue Economy Authority, strengthened regulation, innovative financing, and community empowerment, are essential. Marine protected areas (MPAs) have emerged as a tool to conserve marine biodiversity and support human livelihoods. This paper reviews the global research landscape, the evolution of concepts and the relevance of valuation techniques related to the assessment of the contribution of MPAs to societal welfare. The review indicates that less than 3% of the wider MPA literature explores the economic valuation of MPA designation. Of those, there is an obvious preference for non-market-based methods of valuation. This may be driven by an increased focus on protecting marine biodiversity rather than the ocean economy revenue streams. Results also show that the United Kingdom, the United States, and Australia carry out the majority of MPA valuation research, while Europe exhibits the most active MPA research collaborative network. The results suggest that South America and Africa appear to have minimal MPA research and collaboration networks. Contingent valuation methods and choice experiments are the preferred valuation tools used for MPA ecosystem service benefit estimation.                   <jats:p>
                    Coastal wetlands are increasingly impacted by tropical cyclones and storm surges. Seawalls and levees built to reduce these hazards disconnect wetlands from adjacent uplands, yet their hydroecological effects remain poorly understood. Using continuous hydrological observations in Chongming Island, Changjiang Estuary, China, we compared seaward and landward wetlands separated by a seawall. CTD sensor data, water quality measurements, and plot surveys revealed that seawall construction weakens tidal connectivity and reduces hydrological exchange landward. Seaward wetlands exhibit tidal‐dominated dynamics with higher salinity and lower chlorophyll (CHL), chemical oxygen demand (COD), and total organic carbon (TOC), associated with presence of
                    <jats:italic>Phragmites australis</jats:italic>
                    . Interior wetlands show reduced salinity, higher values of CHL, COD and TOC, stronger rainfall‐driven responses, and are characterized by more terrestrial vegetation species. These findings suggest that seawalls can substantially alter wetland hydrodynamics and ecosystem structure, highlighting the importance of incorporating hydrological connectivity into seawall design to sustain wetland functions.

title: Crossref record doi:10.21425/fob.19.142560: Environmental and geographic predictors of seed plant diversity across South American terrestrial coastal lomas
text:
{"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,12]],"date-time":"2026-10-12T14:44:54Z","timestamp":1791816294955,"version":"4.3.4"},"reference-count":163,"publisher":"Pensoft Publishers","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,12]],"date-time":"2026-10-12T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1791763200000},"content-version":"vor","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"}],"content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"short-container-title":["biogeography"],"abstract":"<jats:p>Understanding the predictors of plant diversity gradients remains a major challenge in biogeography, particularly in understudied arid ecosystems where water availability is highly constrained. Coastal lomas—isolated, fog-fed vegetation oases distributed across the Peruvian and Chilean coastal deserts of South America–provide a unique system for examining how climate, topography, and geography shape plant diversity under extreme aridity. Here, we evaluated the geographic variation and predictors of the taxonomic and phylogenetic diversity of seed plants in these environments. We compiled the most comprehensive data set to date of 71 coastal lomas and used generalized linear models to assess latitudinal diversity gradients. We also evaluated the relative importance of environmental, topographic, and geographic predictors of plant taxonomic and phylogenetic diversity. We found that mean phylogenetic distance (MPD) exhibited non-linear relationships with latitude, and standardized phylogenetic diversity (PD) showed a weak variation with latitude, with both peaking in the hyper-arid core of the Atacama Desert. In contrast, standardized mean nearest taxon distance (MNTD) and species richness (adjusted by area) showed no significant association with latitude. Our results suggest that current climate, environmental heterogeneity, and geographical factors are the primary predictors of seed plant diversity in these regions. Plant species richness (adjusted by area) increased with aridity and cloud cover, while standardized PD decreased with aridity and distance to the coast while increasing with human footprint and northness. Standardized MNTD also increased with human footprint and northness, and decreased with increasing aridity and temperature. Standardized MPD increased with slope, temperature, northness, and aridity, and decreased with cloud cover, isothermality, and distance to the coast. These results suggest that environmental filtering is not the only macroecological process acting on plant diversity across coastal lomas and is often counterbalanced at different points in evolutionary time by factors associated with environmental heterogeneity, possibly reflecting the presence of climate refugia and habitats that promote species coexistence. Over evolutionary time, these factors may have significantly contributed to shaping the current composition of coastal lomas.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Plant diversity did not follow a simple latitudinal gradient across coastal lomas.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Aridity predominantly explains variation in diversity facets, underscoring the importance of water availability in shaping coastal lomas.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Evolutionary diversity reached its peak unexpectedly in the hyper-arid Atacama Desert.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Plant communities were clustered into distinct assemblages that correspond to geographic barriers along the coastal desert.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Coastal lomas reflect multiple ecological and evolutionary processes rather than environmental filtering alone.</jats:p>","DOI":"10.21425/fob.19.142560","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,12]],"date-time":"2026-10-12T13:48:42Z","timestamp":1791812922000},"source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Environmental                     Climate change is altering ecosystems worldwide, but long-term, site-level hydroclimatic responses remain comparatively under-documented in many tropical regions. We analyzed long-term air and water temperature, precipitation, and stream water level data from two active Caribbean research sites: La Selva Research Station, Costa Rica, and El Verde Field Station, Puerto Rico. Our goal was to assess long-term hydroclimatic trends and changes in extreme events using continuous monitoring from automatic and manual sensors. Long-term records show a mean daily temperature of 25.1°C (1992–2024, range: 19.5-29.6°C) at La Selva and 23.6°C (2000–2024, range: 17.7-28.2°C) at El Verde. Mean annual precipitation is 4166 mm at La Selva (1983–2024) and 3635.8 mm at El Verde (1975–2024). We found a decadal warming trend of 0.29°C at both locations. The El Niño Southern Oscillation (ENSO) influenced air temperature at El Verde, where La Niña (+0.02°C day
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    , 95% CI: 0.002–0.042) phase was associated with higher daily temperatures, but had no detectable effect on air temperature at La Selva. A significant increase in the frequency of extreme temperature events (defined as exceeding the 95
                    <jats:sup>th</jats:sup>
                    , 97
                    <jats:sup>th</jats:sup>
                    , and 99
                    <jats:sup>th</jats:sup>
                    percentiles) was observed at both sites. Using the 95
                    <jats:sup>th</jats:sup>
                    percentile and a fitted generalized linear model, both locations had ~8 extreme temperature events per year in the beginning and increased to ~35 events per year in 2024. Changes in precipitation extremes were site-specific and differed between wet and dry metrics. La Selva showed an increase in wet extremes (heavy precipitation), with 99
                    <jats:sup>th</jats:sup>
                    percentile rainfall exceedances rising from ~1 event per year (1983–1985) to 6 per year in 2024. In contrast, El Verde showed no significant increase in heavy-precipitation events, but exhibited an increase in dry extremes (dry days <1.4 mm, increasing from 152 to 170 days per year). Stream water temperature had a moderate but significant increase. At La Selva, water temperature increased by 0.2°C, and at El Verde, by 0.9°C. An increasing tendency in high-water-level conditions was observed at both locations, though with marginal statistical support (p = 0.08 for the 99
                    <jats:sup>th</jats:sup>
                    percentile at La Selva and 95
                    <jats:sup>th</jats:sup>
                    percentile at El Verde), with estimated durations above these extreme thresholds roughly doubling over the study period. Overall, our study shows an increasing frequency of extreme events, both wet and dry, at these two Caribbean protected locations. These findings suggest important and distinct regional changes in climate over the region, with important consequences for ecosystem conservation and management.

However, limited empirical evidence exists on the effects of adoption intensity, particularly when farmers adopt multiple technologies simultaneously. This study examines the effects of CSAT adoption intensity on maize yield and household asset accumulation in Ghana using survey data from 2,151 maize farmers. A dose\u2013response model with Heckman selection is applied to address potential selection bias and estimate the causal effects of varying adoption levels. The findings show that farmers\u2019 education, access to credit, extension services, and perceived drought significantly influence both the likelihood and intensity of CSAT adoption. Results reveal a U-shaped relationship between CSAT adoption intensity and maize yield, where yields initially decline but increase as adoption intensity rises. On average, higher CSAT adoption is associated with a 21% increase in maize yield. Similarly, CSAT intensity shows a nonlinear positive relationship with household asset accumulation, with an average 19.5% increase in assets. The results also indicate heterogeneous effects across farmers. Overall, higher CSAT adoption improves agricultural productivity and long-term household welfare, highlighting the need to strengthen extension services, expand credit access, and raise climate risk awareness to promote sustainable agricultural development.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1371\/journal.pclm.0000886","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,12]],"date-time":"2026-10-12T17:25:02Z","timestamp":1791825902000},"page":"e0000886","update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1371\/journal.pclm.corrections_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["How much climate-smart agriculture is enough?                   <jats:p>This study investigates how the argument structure of shifting verbs in Mandarin is represented and processed during
          sentence comprehension. Shifting verbs — traditionally classified as intransitive but increasingly used in transitive frames — have been
          widely discussed in theoretical linguistics; however, their cognitive status remains underexplored. Addressing this gap, we examine whether
          shifting verbs have developed transitive argument structures and how they are processed in real time. Using self-paced reading and
          acceptability judgments, we compared shifting verbs to unaccusative verbs in transitive and intransitive contexts, where unaccusative,
          traditionally analyzed as intransitive, served as a baseline. Acceptability results showed that shifting verbs in transitive frames were
          readily accepted, unlike unaccusative verbs, which were consistently rejected in the same contexts. Reading time data revealed distinct
          processing profiles: Shifting verbs exhibited argument-structure flexibility, including possible coactivation of transitive and intransitive
          representations at the verb and target regions. In contrast, unaccusative verbs elicited substantial processing penalties in transitive
          frames. These findings show that argument structure representations can be shaped by usage. More broadly, results suggest that grammatical
          change can be observed not only in language use but also in real-time comprehension, offering insights into how evolving syntactic
          configurations are encoded and accessed in the mental lexicon.</jats:p>","DOI":"10.1075/consl.25020.lia","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,12]],"date-time":"2026-10-12T12:05:46Z","timestamp":1791806746000},"source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["When To address the limitation that existing studies primarily focus on single water sources or historical statistical analyses, while lacking quantitative evaluations of synergistic failure risks among multiple water-source projects under future climate scenarios, this study proposes a comprehensive risk assessment framework. Using a typical irrigation district in Jiangsu Province, China, as a case study and daily meteorological data from 1970 to 2017 as the baseline, the proposed framework quantifies the failure probability of existing irrigation rules under future climate scenarios and identifies the corresponding critical failure thresholds. The results indicate that, under the drier IPSL-CM5A-LR climate scenario, the failure probability increases significantly compared with that under the wetter BNU-ESM scenario, with the projected failure occurring 23 years earlier than under the historical baseline conditions. Compared with previous studies on irrigation engineering risk assessment, the proposed framework enables a comprehensive end-to-end evaluation encompassing meteorological drivers, runoff simulation, rule extraction, and failure probability quantification. It therefore provides a transferable decision-support tool for enhancing the climate resilience of agricultural infrastructure in water-receiving Here we present near\u2010terminus observations from three glacierized fjords in southeast Greenland, combining full\u2010depth turbidity profiles and current velocity from summer 2024 to evaluate sediment export. We identify extensive subsurface sediment plumes from marine\u2010terminating glaciers which are undetectable using remote sensing approaches and underrepresented in fjord sediment\u2010core reconstructions. Sediment cores document an exponential increase in sediment accumulation rates from glacier\u2010distal to glacier\u2010proximal coring sites. Therefore, the scarcity of sediment cores collected in the immediate vicinity of glacier termini suggests that sediment export from marine\u2010terminating glaciers has likely been systematically underestimated. Our findings underscore the importance of direct observations for quantifying sediment transport in glacierized fjords and suggest the Greenland Ice Sheet contributes more sediment to ocean margins domain with realistic topography. This can be called a first \u201cglobal large\u2010eddy simulation\u201d (GLES) for deep convection. The resolution dependence across km\u2010 to sub\u2010km scales and sensitivity to turbulence schemes are investigated. The results showed that the too\u2010intense localized precipitation frequently produced in km\u2010scale models, known as \u201cpopcorn\u2010like\u201d precipitation, weakens as resolution increases. Although zonal mean precipitation differs substantially across turbulence schemes at km\u2010scale resolution, it decreases as resolution increases, indicating convergence across the schemes.                   <jats:p>Understanding the variability and evolution of precipitation extremes associated with climate change is essential to support adaptation strategies, risk management, and civil protection. In this context, this study investigates the climatology, observed trends, and future projections of precipitation extremes in the Southeast Atlantic Hydrographic Basin (SAHB), a region of great socioeconomic relevance in Brazil. Daily precipitation data from 244 pluviometric and meteorological stations of the National Water and Basic Sanitation Agency (ANA) and the National Institute of Meteorology (INMET) were used, covering the period from 1980 to 2023. Precipitation extremes were evaluated using standardized indices from the Expert Team on Climate Change Detection and Indices (ETCCDI). Trend detection and assessment in the time series were performed using the non‐parametric Mann–Kendall test and Sen's slope estimator. For the evaluation of future conditions, simulations from the EC‐Earth3 Earth system model, part of CMIP6, were used, considering the SSP2‐4.5 and SSP5‐8.5 emission scenarios for the period 2030–2100. The results indicate a significant increase in the mean rainfall intensity and a longer duration of dry periods (+4 days/decade), suggesting greater irregularity in the regional precipitation regime. Extreme precipitation events over short periods exhibit spatially heterogeneous intensification, with greater intensity in coastal and mountainous regions. Future projections indicate intensified extreme rainfall (up to +41 mm/decade in precipitation above the 95th percentile) and longer dry spells, particularly under the high‐emission scenario, suggesting greater susceptibility to hydrometeorological disasters and significant impacts on water security and territorial planning across the basin.</jats:p>","DOI":"10.1002/joc.70629","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,8]],"date-time":"2026-10-08T13:33:28Z","timestamp":1791466408000},"update-policy":"https://doi.org/10.1002/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Shifting Patterns of Precipitation Extremes in the

Plant Nutr. Soil Sci."],"abstract":"<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>On ca. 10% of the forested sites in the Bavarian Alps (Germany) mountain, forest soils (so‐called folic histosols) are characterized by thick organic layers overlying poorly weathered calcareous parent material.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Aim</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>These organic layers play a critical role in releasing water and nutrients for vegetation, yet they are also sensitive to climate change, with warming‐induced increases in respiration potentially reducing their thickness and water‐holding capacity.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We used the process‐based water balance model LWF‐Brook90 to simulate soil water availability for 117 sites represented by georeferenced folic histosol profiles and to study the effect of different climate change scenarios (Representative Concentration Pathway [RCP] 2.6, 4.5, and 8.5) and humus loss (0%–75%) on the water balance. Specifically, we used high‐resolution climate data and HYPROP‐based Mualem–van Genuchten parameters to study potential changes in soil water retention and drought risk.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Simulating the effects of changes in precipitation and temperature in combination with organic layer degradation and the resultant loss of water‐holding capacity led to significant increases in predicted transpiration deficits. A 50% reduction in organic layer thickness resulted in a distinct decrease of plant‐available moisture even under the optimistic RCP 2.6 scenario. Under severe climate change (scenario RCP 8.5) and 75% organic layer loss, water availability shifted up to two levels on a seven‐part relative scale of moisture regime. Although such extreme levels (>50%) of organic layer loss are unlikely under closed canopy conditions, they may occur following stand‐replacing disturbance events such as large‐scale windthrows or bark‐beetle outbreaks, which are expected to increase under climate change. Drought‐induced reductions of vegetation productivity may inhibit litter production and the replenishment of organic layers.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Our findings highlight the vulnerability of sites dominated by thick organic layers to climate‐driven water stress. By the end of the century, even under an optimistic scenario (no humus loss, RCP 4.5), the site water balance class on folic histosols is projected to decline by one class for the drier sites (75th percentile). Preventing a downward spiral of mountain forests triggered by climate change requires a holistic silvicultural concept for preserving folic histosols.</jats:p>

                  <jats:p>Southwest Asia (SWA) is a climatically sensitive region where water resources are determined by the complex interactions between the Indian Summer Monsoon and Mediterranean winter systems. Coarse‐resolution global climate models (GCMs) have difficulties in capturing the arid‐to‐semi‐arid hydroclimate of the region, which is characterized by high variability and orographically intensified precipitation. This study evaluates the extent to which dynamical downscaling improves the representation of mean and extreme precipitation in SWA. We use the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model at a resolution of 10 km, driven by boundary conditions from the Community Earth System Model (CESM v1.2.2). We compare the atmospheric component of the native CESM (~2° resolution), the downscaled WRF simulation, and ERA5 for the common period 1950–2002, with supplementary validation against two satellite‐gauge blended products, CHIRPS v3.0 and PERSIANN‐CDR v01r01, for 1983–2002. Our analysis reveals three main findings. First, WRF significantly improves the annual cycle of precipitation, closely agreeing with ERA5. Meanwhile CESM has an inverted annual cycle relative to ERA5, substantially underestimating winter precipitation, while showing a summer wet bias. This summer overestimation is also identified in the extreme precipitation of CESM in the southern part of SWA. Second, the spatial patterns of seasonal mean and extreme precipitation generally agree between WRF and ERA5, with WRF correctly identifying the primary precipitation maxima across all seasons, consistent with the locations shown by the satellite products, though WRF consistently overestimates the magnitude and spatial extent of these maxima relative to ERA5. Third, in areas of complex orography, such as the Zagros Mountains, WRF exhibits precipitation values higher than ERA5. This is attributed to the higher‐resolution topographic representation of WRF, which enhances orographic uplift, and its explicit treatment of convection. These findings demonstrate that dynamical downscaling substantially reduces large‐scale GCM biases and provides a more consistent representation of precipitation in a region of complex orography and limited observational data availability.</jats:p>","DOI":"10.1002/joc.70613","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,7]],"date-time":"2026-10-07T06:47:28Z","timestamp":1791355648000},"update-policy":"https://doi.org/10.1002/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Added Value of

Here, we assess 21st\u2010century changes in temperature and precipitation over Mexico using 36 CMIP6 models under four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1\u20102.6, SSP2\u20104.5, SSP3\u20107.0 and SSP5\u20108.5). Model performance was evaluated against CRU and ERA5 for 1981\u20132000 using the Taylor Skill Score, and the five best\u2010performing models were selected to construct a primary multimodel ensemble. Projections from this selected ensemble were compared with those from the complete 36\u2010model ensemble to evaluate the influence of historical model performance on projected climate signals and uncertainty. Results show robust warming across Mexico under all scenarios, with national mean temperature increases reaching approximately 1.7\u00b0C under SSP1\u20102.6 and 4.9\u00b0C under SSP5\u20108.5 by 2081\u20132100. Warming intensifies with radiative forcing, is generally stronger over northern Mexico, and exhibits high inter\u2010model consistency. In contrast, precipitation shows greater temporal, spatial and inter\u2010model variability. National precipitation remains comparatively stable under SSP1\u20102.6 but progressively declines under higher\u2010forcing scenarios, with widespread drying projected across southern and southeastern Mexico. Seasonal analysis indicates that this annual drying signal is primarily associated with reductions during the wet season, whereas dry\u2010season changes remain comparatively small and heterogeneous. The selected and complete ensembles produce similar large\u2010scale temperature and precipitation patterns, but historical model selection reduces inter\u2010model spread and areas of low agreement, particularly for precipitation. Overall, our results show that future climate change in Mexico will be characterized by robust and spatially coherent warming, together with a more uncertain but progressively stronger drying tendency, particularly during the wet title: Crossref record doi:10.3176/arch.2026.2.03: Animal exploitation over two millennia at Aukuras hill hillfort at the Kernavė archaeological complex, Lithuania: zooarchaeological evidence from bird
text: {"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,6]],"date-time":"2026-10-06T13:53:46Z","timestamp":1791294826355,"version":"4.1.0"},"reference-count":123,"publisher":"Estonian Academy Publishers","issue":"2","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,5]],"date-time":"2026-10-05T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1791158400000},"content-version":"unspecified","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http:\/\/creativecommons.org\/licenses\/by\/4.0\/"}],"content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"short-container-title":["EJA"],"published-print":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,5]]},"abstract":"<jats:p>The Kernav\u00c4\u0097 archaeological complex in eastern Lithuania provides a rare opportunity to investigate long-term changes in human\u00e2\u0080\u0093animal relationships within a single site landscape. This paper presents the results of zooarchaeological analyses of 15 339 animal remains recovered from Aukuras hill hillfort in Kernav\u00c4\u0097, of which 4207 were identified to various taxonomic levels, from order and family to species. The assemblage spans four occupation phases between c. 800 cal BC and 1400 cal AD and includes mammals, birds, and fish, allowing the reconstruction of animal husbandry, hunting, and fishing practices over nearly two millennia. The results demonstrate that farming was already fully established during the Late Bronze Age, with pigs and sheep\/goats forming the basis of animal husbandry. During the late Pre-Roman and Roman periods, cattle became increasingly important, likely reflecting the intensification of crop cultivation. The same period yielded the earliest known chicken remains in Lithuania, indicating the introduction of the domestic chicken by c. 200 cal BC\u00e2\u0080\u0093200 cal AD. The medieval assemblage reveals a distinct pattern of elite consumption and hunting. Compared with the inhabitants of Kernav\u00c4\u0097\u00e2\u0080\u0099s medieval Upper and Lower Towns, pork, birds, fish, and wild game appear to have played a more important role in the diet of the residents of Aukuras hill hillfort. The abundance of northern goshawk remains and hare bones points to the importance of falconry and specialised hunting focused on small game. The assemblage provides new insights into the interaction between farming, social status, and animal exploitation in the eastern Baltic from prehistory to the medieval period.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.3176\/arch.2026.2.03","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,5]],"date-time":"2026-10-05T12:26:46Z","timestamp":1791203206000},"page":"159-191","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Animal exploitation over two millennia at Aukuras hill hillfort at the Kernav\u0117 archaeological complex, Lithuania: zooarchaeological evidence from birds, fish, and mammals (c. 800 cal BC\u20131400 cal AD)"],"prefix":"10.3176","volume":"30","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0002-5168-8568","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Giedr\u0117","family":"Pili\u010diauskien\u0117","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0009-2089-5618","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Saulius","family":"Rumbutis","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0002-3619-9686","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Karolis","family":"Minkevi\u010dius","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0003-1502-901X","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Rokas","family":"Vengalis","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0002-9523-7651","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Gintautas","family":"V\u0117lius","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"1761","reference":[{"key":"ref0","doi-asserted-by":"publisher","unstructured":"Anthony, D., Trautmann, M. & Heyd, V. 2026. Although gridded climate products offer a scalable alternative, their ability to capture the co-occurrence of heat and water deficit stress remains poorly evaluated. We address this gap by (i) evaluating four daily rainfall and four maximum air temperature (Tmax) products against observations from four Zambian stations (2013\/14\u20132025\/26) using conventional and confusion-matrix statistics; (ii) applying the best-performing products to characterise concurrent stress at six major production sites across Malawi, Mozambique and Zambia over 41 seasons (1985\/86\u20132025\/26); and (iii) examining associations with ENSO phases and documented droughts. Concurrent stress was defined as hot-dry days (Tmax &gt; 30 \u00b0C and rainfall &lt; 1 mm day\u22121) and hot-dry spells (\u2265 3 consecutive hot-dry days). CHIRPS provided the most accurate rainfall estimates (monthly R\u00b2 up to 0.89; dry-day F1 71.4\u201383.8 %), while MERRA-2 best identified heat-stress days (F1 up to 82.7 %). The CHIRPS\u2013MERRA-2 combination revealed higher stress frequencies at Zambian sites than at Malawian and Mozambican sites. El Ni\u00f1o seasons were associated with significantly greater concurrent stress (p&lt; 0.001). Stress probability peaked in November (0.37\u20130.67), highlighting vulnerability during crop establishment. Validated gridded products can therefore support climate-informed monitoring and decision-making in Southern African rainfed systems.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.2166\/wcc.2026.580","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,2]],"date-time":"2026-10-02T19:32:33Z","timestamp":1790969553000},"update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.2166\/iwapcrossmarkpolicypage","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Evaluating remotely sensed climate products for monitoring ENSO-driven concurrent heat and water-deficit stress in rainfed maize\u2013soybean systems of Southern Africa"],"prefix":"10.2166","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0003-1136-7046","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Emmanuel Muteba","family":"Ngonga","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"a Department of Soil and Environment, Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences, P.O. However, the majority of psychological research ignores or marginalises culture and context. This is problematic because, despite representing a small portion of humanity (specifically Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich and Democratic (WEIRD) populations) mainstream psychology is published as if it represented the whole humanity. Among the subfields of psychology, social psychology is arguably the one in which this issue should be least prevalent. To investigate this, we conducted a study on titles and abstracts of articles from 69 social psychology journals published between 1990 and 2020, examining how cultural diversity and awareness of its importance changed over time. The results indicate that cultural awareness is more prominent in journals focused on culture, international or local issues; while remaining almost entirely absent in journals focused on theory, reviews and business. Furthermore, cultural awareness displays an imbalance regarding culture: while WEIRD mentions remain most common, mentions of other regions appear to be disproportionately represented or \u2018inflated\u2019 in specific contexts. The generalizability of psychological theories will remain impossible if culture is not integrated as a central factor in research.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1002\/ijop.70275","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,2]],"date-time":"2026-10-02T13:44:23Z","timestamp":1790948663000},"update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1002\/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["To Long-term changes in meteorological variables, river runoff, and sea level were assessed using data from 33 hydrometeorological stations and gauging posts for 1981\u20132024. Trends were evaluated using the Mann-Kendall test and Sen\u2019s slope estimator, while atmospheric circulation was examined using the Vangengeim-Girs classification and North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) index. The results indicate significant regional warming, with a mean annual air temperature of approximately 14.0 \u00b0C and an increase of 1.6 \u00b0C over the study period (Sen\u2019s slope: +0.036 \u00b0C\/year). Summer warming was particularly pronounced, reaching 0.73 \u00b0C\/decade in Baku, while August temperature anomalies reached +1.5 \u00b0C relative to the 1961\u20131990 baseline. Total river runoff decreased by 24% (115.5 m\u00b3\/s) during 1991\u20132024 compared with 1961\u20131990, coinciding with persistent sea-level regression. GIS-based analysis indicates that shoreline retreat exposed approximately 1,371.7 km\u00b2 of coastal land, about 60% of which has become stable dry surfaces. Correlation analysis suggests that sea-level variability is associated with large-scale circulation: E-type circulation correlates negatively (r = \u22120.62 to \u22120.67), whereas W-type circulation shows a positive correlation (r = Such incidents have recently become both more frequent and significant in scale and impact (Singh et al., 2016). The primary focus of this study is to examine the short-term effects on valuations and the dynamics of spillover between public and private sector banks. This research examines how the equity market responds to major news of bank fraud, investigating short-term value effects and spill-over dynamics between government-owned and privately owned banks. The findings, based on an enhanced event study combined with regression analysis, suggest that fraud in private banks does not affect the victim bank, but is accompanied by negative spillovers to public sector banks. Additionally, the results show that investment shifts occur within both public and private bank segments following fraud disclosures. These patterns are further interpreted in light of institutional characteristics, such as ownership structure and operational scale. The study provides evidence specific to India on how markets respond to announcements of banking text: {"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,1]],"date-time":"2026-10-01T08:58:19Z","timestamp":1790845099783,"version":"4.1.0"},"reference-count":35,"publisher":"Noyam Publishers","issue":"8","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,30]],"date-time":"2026-09-30T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1790726400000},"content-version":"unspecified","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http:\/\/creativecommons.org\/licenses\/by\/4.0\/"}],"content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"short-container-title":["EHASS"],"abstract":"<jats:p>As generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) models achieve high fidelity in mimicking musical structures and timbres, debates surrounding the role of human agency in listener engagement emerge. As the music industry moves to algorithmic music to ensure efficiency, it is not yet clear whether audiences are appreciating music as an independent sonic entity or as a communicative gesture of human will. This paper examined how perceived authorship affects emotional resonance in Kenyan university students through a mixed-methods explanatory sequential design. The study, anchored in the Theory of Ngoma, which views music as a complete social institution that needs vital force (Roho), questions the belief that acoustic perfection is synonymous with artistic value. A quantitative deceptive listening experiment (N = 76) was conducted across student populations drawn from Kabarak University, Kenyatta University, and the Technical University of Kenya. The qualitative phase employed expert elicitation, in which the insights of an international panel of musicologists, AI experts, and cultural theorists were sought. This professional discussion was employed to address the authenticity loss and to interpret the statistical declines in emotional attachment within the framework of African musicology, formalist aesthetics, and neoliberal commodification. The findings showed that explicit knowledge of AI authorship led to a directional decline in listener emotional resonance, even where the tracks were sonically indistinguishable. This suggests a fundamental audience preference for the human spirit and intentionality behind the sound. Consequently, these findings provide critical insights into the limitations of AI in replicating the functional, socio-spiritual, and communal dimensions of African musical arts.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.38159\/ehass.2026785","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,10,1]],"date-time":"2026-10-01T08:18:07Z","timestamp":1790842687000},"page":"2242","update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.38159\/p2020084","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Does the listener care? Here, we assess SWOT observability of irrigation canal networks across 22 Asian countries using a new confidence level (CL) metric. Validation against in situ gauge observations showed that higher CL corresponds to significantly lower water\u2010level retrieval error. Of approximately 795,110\u00a0km of canals analyzed, 37.5% (297,799\u00a0km) show high confidence, 46.9% (373,035\u00a0km) moderate confidence, and 15.6% (124,276\u00a0km) low confidence of observability. Observability is highest in the Indus Basin, Indo\u2010Gangetic Plain, Bangladesh delta, North China Plain, and parts of Myanmar, the Philippines, Nepal, and the Mekong delta, and lowest across parts of Central Asia. Our analysis indicates SWOT can meaningfully support irrigation canal water monitoring across much of Asia's most intensively irrigated regions and around the The country's reliance on rain\u2010fed agriculture increases its vulnerability to climate\u2010related hazards, underscoring the need to synthesize existing evidence on climate risks and food system vulnerability. This systematic review synthesized scientific evidence on the impacts of climate change on Ethiopia's food systems, identified major climate\u2010related risks and vulnerability factors, and assessed adaptation strategies and their policy implications. Following PRISMA guidelines, peer\u2010reviewed studies were systematically identified from major scientific databases using predefined search terms. After applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, 232 eligible studies were included and synthesized thematically to examine climate risks, vulnerability determinants, food system impacts, and adaptation measures. Evidence from 232 studies indicates that climate variability and climate change are major drivers of food insecurity in Ethiopia. Drought, rising temperatures, and changing rainfall patterns were the principal climate risks affecting agricultural production and food availability. Recurrent droughts accounted for approximately 60% of crop yield losses, food insecurity increased by an estimated 2.3% annually, and a 1\u00b0C rise in temperature was associated with a 10% reduction in major staple crop production. Rural households were disproportionately affected, experiencing 15% greater deterioration in food security than urban households. The reviewed studies consistently identified climate\u2010resilient agricultural practices, irrigation expansion, and region\u2010specific adaptation measures as key strategies for reducing climate\u2010induced food insecurity. Climate change poses substantial risks to Ethiopia's food systems through interacting environmental and socio\u2010economic pathways. Strengthening climate\u2010resilient agriculture, improving water resource management, expanding social protection, and promoting locally appropriate adaptation strategies are essential to enhance food security. These findings provide evidence to inform policy, practice, and future research while highlighting the need to address regional knowledge gaps and evaluate the long\u2010term effectiveness of adaptation interventions.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1002\/pei3.70207","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,30]],"date-time":"2026-09-30T10:01:46Z","timestamp":1790762506000},"update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1002\/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Systematic Drawing on twelve semi\u2010structured interviews conducted across homes, workplaces, and caf\u00e9s in the city, seven of which anchor the primary analysis presented here, it employs a feminist political economy lens and interpretivist methodology to foreground care as a contested terrain rather than a normative moral duty. The analysis reveals how women's labor is organized through moral economies, gendered spatialities, and temporal dispossession, producing forms of exhaustion that are routinized and affectively sanctioned. It situates self\u2010care not as commodified wellness but as a relational act of micro\u2010resistance, theorized through decolonial and affective feminist frameworks. By centering participant testimony, this article reorients care from moral virtue to political struggle, calling for a reconfiguration of care ethics rooted in collective infrastructures that refuse Yet research on climate\u2010policy participation has focused largely on formal participation opportunities, paying less attention to citizens' expectations regarding governance roles and their evaluations of policy processes. This study examines how three survey\u2010derived governance role orientations\u2014governmental, civic, and industry\u2010and\u2010media orientations\u2014and perceived climate policy governance quality are associated with two participation outcomes: institutional participation intention and climate\u2010related civic participation behavior. The analysis uses data from a nationwide quota\u2010based online survey of 500 adults in South Korea and applies hierarchical regression models. Civic orientation is positively associated with both participation outcomes, whereas governmental orientation is negatively associated with institutional participation intention. Industry\u2010and\u2010media orientation is not significantly associated with either outcome. Perceived climate policy governance quality is positively associated with both institutional participation intention and civic participation behavior, but none of its interactions with the three orientations is statistically significant. The findings distinguish citizens' expectations about governance roles from their evaluations of governance\u2010process quality. They suggest that civic orientation and favorable process evaluations operate as separate and largely additive correlates of climate\u2010policy participation. Effective participation strategies should therefore combine meaningful institutional openness with durable connections to citizen\u2010 and civil society\u2010led climate                   <jats:p>
                    Sea level rise is causing the rapid conversion of upland habitats to salt marshes in low‐sloping areas due to increasing groundwater salinity and soil saturation. Despite this being a widespread phenomenon, questions remain about the factors shaping groundwater hydrology and salinity in these transitioning systems, particularly in the US Northeast. We examined water table elevations and specific conductivity (a proxy for salinity) in three northeastern forests with differing slopes where forest retreat has been occurring at rates of approximately 1 m yr
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    over the past 100 years. Our results indicate that water table levels were impacted by seasons, storms, precipitation and soil characteristics. Water tables were significantly higher during the dormant season than the growing season at all sites. Water table elevation relative to mean high water was approximately equal at all sites across the marsh–forest ecotone, with two key implications. First, forests on steeper terrain had a deeper water table. Second, because the overall hydraulic gradient was low, even sites with steeper slopes remain vulnerable to saltwater intrusion. Salinity dynamics were occasionally driven by storm surges and hydraulic gradients, but the magnitude and direction of these effects were not consistent across events. Finally, sites with greater soil hydraulic conductivity exhibited greater depths to the water table and enhanced tidal advection. This pattern suggests that well‐drained soils characteristic of the Pine Barrens Ecoregion may facilitate efficient drainage but simultaneously heighten susceptibility to saltwater intrusion. These findings underscore the need to consider local hydrologic and soil conditions when predicting the pace of marsh migration and the resilience of coastal forests under rising sea levels.

                  <jats:p>
                    Historical peatland drainage resulted in surface subsidence and reduced water storage capacity (WSC), a process that can be exacerbated by climate change. We assessed the effects of rewetting on WSC using mesocosm experiments in climate chambers, field measurements, and Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) analysis. Results showed that rewetting significantly increased WSC under both present and future RCP 4.5 climates, with stronger effects where
                    <jats:italic>Sphagnum moss</jats:italic>
                    recovery may restore surface porosity. Rewetting enhances WSC under shallow antecedent water levels (WLs) and high precipitation, despite reduced vertical storage, due to living
                    <jats:italic>Sphagnum moss</jats:italic>
                    and porous near‐surface peat. Field validation confirmed increased WSC adjacent to the original ditches. In addition, InSAR analysis detected accelerated peat uplift post‐rewetting compared with pristine peatland conditions. These results demonstrate that rewetting effectively restores the flood control function of drained boreal peatlands, strengthens their resilience under climate change, and supports ecosystem recovery and climate adaptation strategies.

title: Crossref record doi:10.1029/2026gc013127: OIB‐Type Garnet Amphibolites From the Xuerongzangbu Area, Central Lhasa Terrane, Tibet: Implications for Songduo Paleo‐Tethys Ocean Evolution and Perm

{"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,29]],"date-time":"2026-09-29T09:59:13Z","timestamp":1790675953982,"version":"4.1.0"},"reference-count":151,"publisher":"American Geophysical Union (AGU)","issue":"10","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,29]],"date-time":"2026-09-29T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1790640000000},"content-version":"vor","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"},{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,29]],"date-time":"2026-09-29T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1790640000000},"content-version":"tdm","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http://doi.wiley.com/10.1002/tdm_license_1.1"}],"content-domain":{"domain":["agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com"],"crossmark-restriction":true},"short-container-title":["Geochem Geophys Geosyst"],"published-print":{"date-parts":[[2026,10]]},"abstract":"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Whether the Songduo metamorphic belt represents an in situ Paleo‐Tethyan suture within the Lhasa Terrane or far‐traveled allochthonous high‐pressure slices, and how Permian mantle activity along the North Gondwana margin relates to subsequent Tethyan evolution, remain central questions in Tibetan tectonics. We investigated retrogressed garnet amphibolites from the Xuerongzangbu area of the Central Lhasa Terrane using petrography, mineral and whole‐rock geochemistry, Sr–Nd isotopes, SHRIMP zircon U–Pb geochronology,
                    <jats:sup>40</jats:sup>
                    Ar/
                    <jats:sup>39</jats:sup>
                    Ar thermochronology, and phase‐equilibrium modeling. The rocks record prograde burial, peak high‐pressure amphibolite‐facies metamorphism, and fluid‐assisted retrogression during exhumation. Modeling of a weakly retrogressed Type I amphibolite yields peak conditions of 15.4–16.0 kbar and 600–660°C, whereas more strongly retrogressed Type II amphibolites preserve relict kyanite, high‐Si amphibole, phengite, and rutile. The amphibolites' OIB‐type trace‐element patterns, initial
                    <jats:sup>87</jats:sup>
                    Sr/
                    <jats:sup>86</jats:sup>
                    Sr ratios of 0.7050–0.7057, ε
                    <jats:sub>Nd</jats:sub>
                    (t) values of −1.59 to +0.16, and Nd model ages of 0.97–1.08 Ga indicate derivation from an enriched intraplate mantle source with limited crustal contamination. Zircon U–Pb dating gives a protolith crystallization age of 271.0 ± 3.0 Ma, whereas hornblende and mica
                    <jats:sup>40</jats:sup>
                    Ar/
                    <jats:sup>39</jats:sup>
                    Ar ages of 232.9–216.9 Ma record Late Triassic cooling and exhumation. Integrated with regional geological evidence, the protoliths are interpreted as seamount or ocean‐island basalts formed on the Songduo oceanic lithosphere. Together with regional Permian plume‐affinity mafic magmatism, these data suggest sustained mantle heating beneath North Gondwana and a possible temporal and geodynamic link between Songduo Ocean closure and the development of younger Tethyan branches.

It aims to enhance radar\u2010based precipitation forecasting, which typically struggles with decreasing accuracy over lead time due to its inability to account for precipitation GD processes. The research focusses on the orographic effect, where moist air rising over elevated terrain leads to enhanced precipitation. The analysis employs a Lagrangian framework to track precipitation systems and quantifies precipitation GD using a logarithmic approach. Various factors were stratified to understand their influence on precipitation GD patterns, including spatial window sizes and lead times, the direction and speed of storms, and air temperature. The results showed that topography plays a paramount role, with most precipitation growth occurring on windward slopes and decay in leeward areas. The study confirmed a strong directional dependence, with most precipitation in GB originating from the west and southwest, leading to enhanced precipitation in the west part of Wales, the Pennines and Scotland. The results also showed that precipitation growth is enhanced with increasing storm speeds, indicating greater dynamic interaction with terrain. Temperature also modulates precipitation GD, with warmer conditions (above 15\u00b0C) showing more widespread precipitation growth. These results provide a framework for incorporating orographic effects and dynamic precipitation evolution into nowcasting models. The study provides insights that are meaningful for future work aimed at improving precipitation GD in nowcasting systems, also critical for flood forecasting and severe\u2010weather The study aims to assess whether digital public service maturity is associated with SME labour productivity and whether this association persists after accounting for economic development. The analysis combines 2022 World Bank GovTech indicators and the United Nations Online Service Index with Eurostat SME productivity data for 2022\u20132023 and World Bank GDP per capita data for 2022 across 33 European countries. SME productivity is measured as value added per person employed; digital service maturity is represented by the Public Service Delivery Index (PSDI) and the Online Service Index (OSI) for 2022. The main hypothesis is that higher digital public service maturity is positively associated with SME productivity and remains significant after controlling for GDP per capita. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, ordinary least squares models, HC3 robust standard errors, diagnostics, and sensitivity analysis are applied. No statistically significant association between PSDI and SME productivity is identified. OSI is positive and significant in bivariate models, but its coefficient is no longer statistically significant after GDP per capita at purchasing power parity is included. Several service-specific GovTech indicators show pronounced ceiling effects and limited variation. The findings indicate that country-level digital service maturity scores should not be treated as stand-alone indicators of the productivity conditions faced by SMEs. Monitoring frameworks should complement maturity scores with measures of business uptake, interoperability, reliability, processing time, and administrative cost savings. The study\u2019s originality lies in jointly demonstrating the specification sensitivity of the OSI\u2013SME productivity association and the limited discriminatory capacity of service-specific GovTech indicators affected by ceiling effects. The conclusions are limited to the analysed indicators and sample and do not establish causal effects; future research should use repeated GovTech observations, purchasing-power-adjusted productivity measures, and firm-level service-use data. title: Crossref record doi:10.38159/erats.20261281: Negotiating the sacred: A pneumatological hermeneutic of syncretism in African Pentecostalism
text: {"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,30]],"date-time":"2026-09-30T17:57:03Z","timestamp":1790791023457,"version":"4.1.0"},"reference-count":66,"publisher":"Noyam Publishers","issue":"8","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,28]],"date-time":"2026-09-28T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1790553600000},"content-version":"unspecified","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http:\/\/creativecommons.org\/licenses\/by\/4.0\/"}],"content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"short-container-title":["ERATS"],"abstract":"<jats:p>This paper examines syncretism in African Pentecostalism using a decolonial pneumatological lens. African Pentecostalism, Charismatics, and neo-Pentecostal movements pursue a distinct pneumatological spirituality, rooted in both indigenous cosmologies and global Pentecostal theology. This article employed qualitative desktop research and used syncretism as a conceptual framework. The findings reveal a departure from Western critiques which frame syncretic practices as theological compromise.  Thus, African Pentecostal syncretism uses a Spirit-led negotiation between indigenous cosmology and global Pentecostal theology. The study concludes that syncretism in African Pentecostalism is a decolonial negotiation, not theological compromise. A pneumatological hermeneutic validates hybrid practices, providing a platform for prayers and deliverance against ancestral influences. The article recommends a pneumatological hermeneutic that validates hybrid spiritual practices as legitimate expressions of faith that are tailored to reclaim African agency and militate against Eurocentric ideas of pure Christianity. This study contributes to reconceptualises syncretism as a decolonial practice in African Pentecostalism.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.38159\/erats.20261281","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,30]],"date-time":"2026-09-30T17:16:03Z","timestamp":1790788563000},"page":"332","update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.38159\/p2020084","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Negotiating the sacred: A pneumatological hermeneutic of syncretism in African Pentecostalism"],"prefix":"10.38159","volume":"12","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0008-5782-762X","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Lyton","family":"Chandomba","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"Apostolic Faith Mission International Ministries, United Kingdom"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0002-4177-8391","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Nomatter","family":"Sande","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[{"id":[{"id":"https:\/\/ror.org\/048cwvf49","id-type":"ROR","asserted-by":"publisher"}],"name":"University of South Africa"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"25245","published-online":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,28]]},"reference":[{"key":"ref0","unstructured":"Alexander, Kimberly Ervin. \u201c\u2018Singing Heavenly Music\u2019: R. This has historically made it difficult for practitioners to reach consensus on ideal management prescriptions and restoration activities. Forest management to decrease wildfire susceptibility and improve water supply is often informed by estimates of live fuel moisture (LFM). However, ecosystem response to environmental conditions and management treatments is dependent to a large degree on soil moisture. Soil moisture has been used as a surrogate to estimate LFM, but tree\u2010based sensors have not been applied in the same manner. In this paired watershed study, coupled soil and tree moisture probes were installed to study the relationship between soil and tree moisture and to examine soil moisture\u2013tree\u2013ecosystem relationships in Sonoma County, CA, USA. We found that (1) there were statistically significant effects on soil moisture and evapotranspiration (ET) from mechanical tree thinning and prescribed burns compared to an untreated watershed, (2) soil moisture decreased at the surface and increased in the root zone post\u2010treatment, relative to an untreated watershed, and (3) ET decreased by 90\u2009mm in the post treatment year for the treated watershed. To investigate regional generalizability of these results, the soil moisture surrogate was applied at a nearby station within the Pepperwood Preserve to look at wildfire danger for large historical fires and was found to be relevant to the surrounding area. These results suggest that in\u00a0situ soil and tree moisture sensors can be used as a surrogate for discrete and time\u2010consuming LFM measurements and that soil moisture thresholds can be used to help identify wildfire susceptibility and drought conditions. Information on the hydrologic response to forest treatment in different locations is valuable to land and resource managers and improving real\u2010time wildfire danger and drought conditions using existing or low\u2010cost in\u00a0situ sensors can improve situational awareness and planning.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1002\/eco.70277","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,28]],"date-time":"2026-09-28T23:20:53Z","timestamp":1790637653000},"update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1002\/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["From Soil to Canopy: Using Moisture Data From Soil and Tree Sensors to Predict Live Fuel Moisture and Guide Forest Management in a Mediterranean Coastal Woodland"],"prefix":"10.1002","volume":"19","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0003-3030-7065","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Michelle","family":"Stern","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"Delta Stewardship Council  Sacramento California USA"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Ryan","family":"Ferrell","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[{"name":"Pepperwood Preserve  Santa Rosa California USA"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Lorraine","family":"Flint","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[{"name":"Earth Systems Modeling Earth Knowledge Inc.                   <jats:p>
                    Wildfires are becoming increasingly frequent and severe as a consequence of climate change. Their impacts on terrestrial ecosystems and on the atmosphere include the release of gases and ash, as well as enhanced soil susceptibility to erosion and the downstream transport of materials into aquatic systems. However, the effects of such disturbances on aquatic ecosystems remain poorly understood. In this study, we assessed short‐ and medium‐term limnological and biological responses of a tropical reservoir located in the Brazilian Cerrado (Lobo–Broa Reservoir) following a large‐scale wildfire. We conducted intensive weekly sampling during the first 5 weeks after the fire, embedded within a longer‐term monthly time series spanning 2 years prior to and 2 years after the disturbance. We hypothesized that the wildfire would have an impact on water transparency, suspended particulate matter, nutrient dynamics, and dissolved organic matter, with cascading effects on planktonic communities. We observed short‐term responses across multiple physical, chemical, and biological variables, although their timing and magnitude differed among ecosystem components. Most parameters returned to their pre‐disturbance trajectories within days to weeks. However, turbidity, euphotic depth, and the abundance of
                    <jats:italic>Synechococcus</jats:italic>
                    ‐like picocyanobacteria and cladocerans showed more persistent deviations extending beyond the immediate post‐fire period. Multivariate analyses revealed that post‐fire samples largely fell within the natural seasonal and interannual variability of the system. Spatial comparisons between nearshore and the pelagic zone indicated differences in variables such as phytoplankton biomass, dissolved oxygen concentration, total phosphorus, fulvic‐like organic matter, and the abundance of cyanobacteria and cladocerans. Overall, the wildfire was associated with detectable changes in limnological conditions and planktonic communities. Nevertheless, most variables exhibited a high degree of resilience over time.

title: Crossref record doi:10.38159/erats.20261284: The irony of law and faith in corruption
text: {"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,28]],"date-time":"2026-09-28T19:57:17Z","timestamp":1790625437279,"version":"4.1.0"},"reference-count":39,"publisher":"Noyam Publishers","issue":"8","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,26]],"date-time":"2026-09-26T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1790380800000},"content-version":"unspecified","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http:\/\/creativecommons.org\/licenses\/by\/4.0\/"}],"content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"short-container-title":["ERATS"],"abstract":"<jats:p>This study examined the pervasive issue of corruption within secular and religious institutions, aiming to understand how these systems, which ought to uphold justice and virtue, can be manipulated for selfish interests. The study used a doctrinal approach to review the literature and explore the motivations behind corruption in both legal and faith-based organisations. The findings reveal a significant disconnect between the ideals of law and faith-based actions, a total dichotomy from societal norms and natural justice. Additionally, legal loopholes are frequently exploited, allowing unethical behaviour to thrive, while religious leaders sometimes misuse their authority, betraying the trust of their congregations. Corruption erodes public trust in institutions designed to serve society, confidence, and the willingness to question. This growing disillusionment can lead to apathy toward civic responsibilities, diminished participation in democratic processes, and a culture of cynicism that undermines social cohesion and stability. Furthermore, the paper highlighted the need for reforms focused on ethical leadership to restore integrity. The study recommends fostering a culture of accountability to bridge the gap between the principles of law and faith and their applications. Contributions of this study to scholarship include innovative mechanisms to eradicate corruption in both secular and religious contexts, strengthened oversight, the implementation of educational reforms that promote trust and accountability, and the reestablishment of boni mores in the broader society.
