We develop a framework to explain how the character of communities influence social and other public services provided by local governments and why rural\u2013urban differences may exist. Theoretically, our framework links conceptualizations of place character with welfare state theory. We illustrate our framework using original primary data collected for 1086 counties spanning the USA. The character of communities varies along economic, sociopolitical, and governmental lines. These same factors influence the services that county governments provide, with results for sociopolitical factors and local government capacity tending to follow welfare state theory. But contrary to views of a binary metro\u2010nonmetro divide: big\u2010city metro counties diverge most from others, especially remote rural counties, and possess characteristics that make them much better equipped to protect the local social safety net even as they engage in competitive economic development; suburban metros are closer to their nonmetro counterparts in service provision and governance; and counties overall face operating pressures. Our findings indicate that future work should consider spatial inequality in the social safety net across graduations of rural\u2013urban communities and whether gaps with big\u2010city metros are intensifying.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1111\/ruso.70070","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,26]],"date-time":"2026-09-26T07:25:53Z","timestamp":1790407553000},"update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1002\/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Place Character and the Local Welfare State: Counties' Social Services and Public Provisions Across Rural and Urban Communities"],"prefix":"10.1111","volume":"91","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0001-7823-8500","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Paige","family":"Kelly","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"Department of Agricultural Economics, Sociology and Education The Pennsylvania State University  University Park Pennsylvania USA"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0003-4946-5936","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Linda M.","family":"Lobao","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[{"name":"Rural Sociology Program, School of Environment and Natural Resources The Ohio State University  Columbus Ohio USA"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"311","published-online":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,26]]},"reference":[{"key":"e_1_2_12_2_1","doi-asserted-by":"publisher","DOI":"10.1177\/0160323X20932624"},{"key":"e_1_2_12_3_1","doi-asserted-by":"publisher","DOI":"10.1111\/cico.12399"},{"key":"e_1_2_12_4_1","volume-title":"Places in Need: The Changing Geography of Poverty","author":"Allard S.","year":"2017"},{"key":"e_1_2_12_5_1","volume-title":"The Case for Growth Centers: How to Spread Tech Innovation Across America","author":"Atkinson R.                     <jats:bold>Background</jats:bold>
                    : Natural history collections can be a valuable source of genetic material for evolutionary research. However, numerous samples from zoological collections are fixed in formalin and may remain continuously exposed to formalin over long periods of time. Due to severe DNA degradation caused by formalin fixation, extracting DNA from these collections is highly challenging.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Results</jats:bold>
                    : Multiple DNA extraction protocols were tested for their ability to recover genetic material from long-term formalin-preserved specimens. We identified a best-performing protocol that provides a straightforward and contamination-resistant method for obtaining high-quality mitochondrial DNA from arthropods, particularly ground beetles (Carabidae) and freshwater crabs (Potamidae), preserved in formalin for up to four decades. Out of the 37 tested samples, 26 produced DNA concentrations of ≥ 0.1 ng/µl at ~ 180 bp (including adapters) after library preparation, which is sufficient for successful Illumina sequencing. Notably, crab samples yielded higher DNA concentrations after library preparation than beetle samples, likely due to differences in tissue structure and preservation history. Results from competitive mapping showed mitochondrial genome coverage ranging from approximately 3X to 17X, despite low endogenous mitochondrial DNA content. Despite the relatively low coverage, the recovered mitochondrial data proved sufficient for downstream phylogenetic analyses. As species-specific genomes were unavailable, coverage was calculated by mapping to the mitochondrial reference genomes of closely-related species of the target taxa.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:bold>Conclusion</jats:bold>
                    : This study demonstrates that high-throughput sequencing is feasible from invertebrate museum specimens preserved in formalin for decades and provides a practical protocol adaptable to a broad taxonomic range.

                    Climate change has accelerated devastating impacts across the globe, and heatwaves are among the most severe climate extremes threatening human health, agricultural productivity, and ecosystems in northwestern Nigeria. This study aimed to develop a long short-term memory (LSTM) based model to predict heatwave trends in northwestern Nigeria. Historical meteorological data, including daily maximum temperature, minimum temperature, and relative humidity from 1980 to 2024, were sourced from the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet). Heatwave intensity was measured via heat index (HI) computation, whereas temporal trends were analyzed via the Modified Mann Kendall (MMK) test and Innovative Trend Analysis (ITA). Spatial variation in heatwave intensity was mapped via the Inverse Distance Weighting (IDW) method. The LSTM model demonstrated high predictive accuracy during the testing phase, with correlation coefficients (R) ranging from 0.87 to 0.91 and coefficients of determination (R
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    ) ranging from 0.76 to 0.83. The findings revealed a pronounced increase in the frequency and severity of heatwaves across northwestern Nigeria. These findings demonstrate the ability of LSTM based forecasting to provide reliable heatwave predictions and highlight the potential of LSTM models for supporting regional climate adaptation strategies, heat early warning systems, and evidence-based decision making.

This faith, they claim, has always spoken metaphysically, until lately challenged by the likes of Heidegger and Marion. However, when we consider Heidegger and Marion's account, we find a completely different approach to metaphysics. For them, \u201cmetaphysics\u201d is about modern metaphysics, defined with a view towards explaining the \u201cdevastation\u201d of modern European and American society, its loss of religion, its wars, its technological and environmental decimation, and its philosophical and theological failures. This article revisits this debate and contends that until a more accurate understanding of Heidegger is achieved, no genuine debate on the nature of \u201cmetaphysics\u201d is possible. To that end, I present the arguments of Betz and Falque, provide a more substantive engagement with Heidegger's thought on metaphysics, and then conclude with further implications for theology in its relation to text: {"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,25]],"date-time":"2026-09-25T13:00:18Z","timestamp":1790341218266,"version":"4.1.0"},"reference-count":80,"publisher":"Noyam Publishers","issue":"7","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,23]],"date-time":"2026-09-23T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1790121600000},"content-version":"unspecified","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http:\/\/creativecommons.org\/licenses\/by\/4.0\/"}],"content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"short-container-title":["EHASS"],"abstract":"<jats:p>Community involvement in post-apartheid South Africa is marked by symbolic engagement and persistent power imbalances that marginalise Indigenous viewpoints and epistemologies. Drawing on decolonial theory, Indigenous Research Methodologies (IRMs), Ubuntu philosophy and Foucauldian discourse analysis, the article discusses how Indigenous epistemology can help reimagine community engagement. In this study, the Meraka Cultural Village in the Free State, South Africa, was used as a case study to demonstrate how practices embedded in the community, rooted locally and involving everyone, can disrupt existing knowledge hierarchies and secure epistemic justice. Data was collected using semi-structured interviews, focus groups, and participant observation, and thematically analysed with an emphasis on power\/knowledge dynamics. The results indicate that Meraka is a community where members take back control of their lives and the wisdom of the older generation is celebrated, and partnerships between the university and the community are strengthened through respect and sharing. Ubuntu provides a theoretical and practical basis for co-creation, trust, and collective well-being. Notwithstanding the persistence of institutional obstacles and discursive silences, Meraka helps create resistance, reflexivity and alternative ways of engagement that challenge the traditional top-down system. The idea of \u201cpockets of hope\u201d reflects how using Indigenous methods and Ubuntu thinking can bring decolonial prospects into community engagement. This study promotes a shift towards relational ethics and pedagogical transparency, positioning Indigenous individuals as equal partners in knowledge production and societal transformation. This enhances broader dialogues on decolonising academia and advancing socially equitable, inclusive engagement strategies within and beyond South Africa\u2019s higher education However, heavily crevassed regions are challenging to survey using conventional methods, leading to data gaps. We establish a passive seismic approach exploiting naturally occurring crevassing events recorded with a dense seismic array to image the ice\u2013bed interface without spatial interpolation. Using P\u2010wave reflections from shallow events detected by matched field processing, we derive a two\u2010dimensional ice\u2010thickness map with \u223c15\u00a0m vertical resolution in a crevasse field on Isunnguata Sermia, West Greenland. Our measurements are consistent with ground\u2010penetrating radar ice thickness picks and extend coverage to previously inaccessible areas. The resolved bed shows a \u223c100\u00a0m deep overdeepening along ice flow, poorly resolved in large\u2010scale bed elevation products, co\u2010located with a previously inferred active subglacial lake. This method provides a robust, logistically simpler tool than more conventional radar and active seismic surveys for high\u2010resolution bed imaging in dynamically active glacier Recent studies have shown that Large Language Models (LLMs) can operate as pattern\u2010recognition systems capable of handling novel domains and purely numerical tasks. Here, we assess the utility of LLMs for earthquake characterization and propose a novel approach based on a small LLM called TinyLlama. We adapt the LLM for seismology through fine\u2010tuning on a subset of Italian earthquakes using the LoRA technique, which involves retraining only about  of the model parameters. Our method takes station coordinates, P\u2010wave arrival times, and peak ground velocities in a small window (0.2\u00a0s) around the P\u2010wave and accurately estimates earthquake magnitude, location, and origin time without using a seismic velocity model. To explore the potential for rapid characterization, we consider only stations where the P\u2010wave arrives within 5\u00a0s of the first triggered station. Compared to standard automatic methods currently used by INGV in Italy our model achieves comparable performance in magnitude estimation and superior accuracy in epicenter, hypocenter and origin time estimation. Validation using both P\u2010 and S\u2010waves shows only a slight performance improvement that does not justify the additional latency. We explored a range of data splitting strategies and found that the LLM\u2010based seismic method is robust. Our results highlight the ability of LLMs to function as effective tools in seismology and suggest their potential for advancing data\u2010driven approaches to rapid earthquake                   <jats:p>
                    Accurately capturing the spatial distribution of precipitation over complex terrain remains a major challenge in meteorology. Satellite observations struggle to simultaneously achieve both high spatiotemporal resolution and retrieval accuracy, while radar observations are easily affected by terrain blockage in mountainous areas. As a result, a single data source is insufficient for high‐resolution precipitation monitoring. In this study, we developed a U‐Net–based deep learning fusion framework incorporating digital elevation model (DEM) information as a terrain constraint. Using hourly GPM IMERG satellite precipitation, SWAN QPE radar precipitation, and rain‐gauge observations collected over Chongqing, China, during the rainy seasons (April–October) of 2016–2021, three multi‐source fusion schemes were constructed: GModel (satellite + gauges), QModel (radar + gauges), and GQModel (satellite + radar + gauges). The performance of the two original precipitation products and the three fused products was comprehensively evaluated. The results show that GPM IMERG tends to overestimate precipitation, and the peak time of precipitation is delayed by approximately 1 h. Although its overall performance is inferior to that of SWAN QPE, the radar product generally underestimates precipitation because of terrain blockage, with substantially better performance over the relatively flat western hills than over the mountainous eastern region in Chongqing. All three fusion products exhibit markedly better agreement with rain‐gauge observations than the original satellite and radar products in both temporal evolution and precipitation magnitude, effectively reducing the systematic biases associated with complex terrain. The generalisation capability of the proposed framework was further evaluated using independent observations from April to October 2023 together with two representative heavy rainfall events that occurred over the western hilly region and the northeastern mountainous region, respectively. The fused precipitation products successfully reproduced both the temporal evolution and rainfall magnitude observed by rain gauges. Overall, GQModel achieved the best comprehensive statistical performance, whereas QModel showed superior skill in estimating extreme precipitation events (> 40 mm h
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    and representative heavy rainfall cases).

We assimilate node\u2010level SWOT WSE into a large\u2010scale hydrodynamic model over the Ohio River Basin using an ensemble Kalman filter and test river\u2010network\u2010aware localization. Assimilation improves discharge skill at most of the 66 USGS gages, including sites without direct SWOT overpasses, with \u223c60% showing higher KGE and ~3% degrading. These improvements suggest that SWOT WSE assimilation extends beyond direct observations, with localization adding benefit. Impacts are governed by transferable constraints, including quality control (QC), residual observation uncertainty, and river\u2010network context. Comparison with SWOT\u2010derived discharge at 27 overlap sites provides complementary context and supports using WSE as a direct hydrodynamic constraint. This study presents an analysis of EPEs across the full annual cycle of the Himalayas from 1979 to 2023, identifying their spatial and seasonal distributions and associated precursor weather regimes. Based on the frequency of seasonal EPEs, the Himalayas are categorized into winter\u2010dominated (Karakoram, WH, and northwest Central Himalayas [CH]) and summer\u2010dominated (CH to Eastern Himalayas [EH]). By clustering circulation fields during EPEs, six dominant weather regimes are identified: four monsoon\u2010driven (Bay of Bengal Low\u2010Pressure System [BoB\u2010LPS], Arabian Sea LPS [AS\u2010LPS], Monsoon\u2010Break, and Western\u2010Disturbance Monsoon [WD\u2010Monsoon]) and two winter\u2010driven (WH\u2010WD and CH\u2010WD). Each regime exhibits a distinct atmospheric circulation pattern. The BoB\u2010LPS and AS\u2010LPS regimes are characterized by quasi\u2010stationary blocking by an anomalous upper\u2010level anticyclone situated over the WH along with the LPS formed over the BoB and AS, respectively. The Monsoon\u2010Break cluster reflects a weakened monsoon trough and suppressed convection over the BoB and core monsoon regions. In contrast, the WH\u2010WD and CH\u2010WD clusters are associated with upper\u2010level cyclonic anomalies characteristic of WDs, embedded within broader wave\u2010train\u2010like circulation anomalies that are consistent with previously reported North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO)\u2013subtropical jet (STJ)\u2013WD pathways. There is a spatial dipole in composite precipitation: EPEs in monsoon\u2010driven clusters are associated with anomalous moisture transport from the BoB and AS, which results in dry conditions in the winter\u2010dominated Himalayas, while EPEs in WD\u2010driven regimes result from anomalous westerly moisture flow from the AS and associated dry conditions in the summer\u2010dominated Himalayas. This study offers a synoptic\u2010scale framework for interpreting the circulation regimes associated with Himalayan EPEs and for identifying conditions that may be favourable for their occurrence.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1002\/qj.70308","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,17]],"date-time":"2026-09-17T09:02:17Z","timestamp":1789635737000},"update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1002\/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Synoptic and large\u2010scale drivers of extreme precipitation events in the Himalayas"],"prefix":"10.1002","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0003-8223-9399","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Priya","family":"Bharati","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"Centre for Ocean, River, Atmosphere and Land Sciences (CORAL) Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur  Kharagpur India"},{"name":"Department of Atmospheric Sciences National Taiwan University  Taipei Taiwan"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0002-1858-0918","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Pranab","family":"Deb","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[{"name":"Centre for Ocean, River, Atmosphere and Land Sciences (CORAL) Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur  Kharagpur India"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0003-1480-3755","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Kieran M. The proposed control strategy aims to minimize energy consumption while maintaining rapid and stable cooling performance under varying ambient conditions. A detailed thermal model of the deep freezer was established using an equivalent resistance\u2013capacitance network representation, enabling precise analysis of temperature dynamics. The sliding mode-based control algorithm dynamically adjusts the compressor\u2019s operating frequency according to temperature deviation, ambient conditions, and time-dependent factors, providing robust performance without requiring parameter retuning for different models. Beyond theoretical-based analysis, a significant contribution of this work is the implementation and validation of the proposed controller in a real experimental test setup, conducted in climate-controlled cold test chambers that comply with international refrigerator testing standards. These tests were conducted in climate-controlled environments in 16\u03bf\u00a0C, 32\u03bf\u00a0C and 43\u03bf\u00a0C, validating the effectiveness of the model. The proposed method achieved up to 26% improvement in freezing capacity and a 12% reduction in the energy efficiency index relative to conventional control strategies. In this paper, we propose a reparameterized transformer framework that integrates High-Rank Factorization (HRF) during training, layer merging at inference, and dynamic, load-balanced distributed inference across multiple devices. To further reduce resource usage, our framework supports mixed-precision quantization down to 4-bit, enabling flexible accuracy\u2013latency\u2013energy trade-offs. Experimental evaluations on the ESC-50 environmental sound dataset demonstrate that our method matches or exceeds the performance of larger baseline models while using 20\u201330% fewer parameters, achieving up to 48% latency reduction in multidevice setups, and substantially lowering energy consumption. Ablation studies confirm the benefits of tuning factorization rank, partition strategy, and quantization level for diverse edge scenarios. While previous studies have considered the effects of participation on citizens' assembly members' attitudes and behaviour, there have been few studies on climate assemblies (see Andrews 2022). This is an important gap as the number for meaningful climate action to be implemented. Moreover, most studies have not provided longitudinal analysis, rely on quantitative data only and are experimental. In this paper, we explore the long\u2010term impacts of participating in a climate assembly on the assembly members' climate knowledge, views, political engagement and consumption behaviours. We draw on a mixed method study that included survey data collected from members of Climate Assembly UK (CAUK) during and after the assembly, and interview data collected shortly after the assembly's conclusion to explore the underlying reasons for changes in a real case. We show that assembly members were more concerned about climate change and were more likely to engage in climate\u2010conscious consumption habits following CAUK than before the assembly. Notably, these changes were evident 12 and 29\u2009months after the end of the assembly, suggesting that members maintained the new habits and attitudes that formed following CAUK's conclusion. This paper contributes to debates about the role of citizens in climate                   <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Interpersonal functioning has a complex, bidirectional relationship with mental disorders such as anxiety and depression. The Inventory of Interpersonal Problems (IIP) assesses aspects of interpersonal functioning, including general interpersonal distress and interpersonal styles. In this study, we aimed to better understand how these aspects relate to anxiety and depression by (1) comparing interpersonal distress and style in individuals with current, past, and no lifetime anxiety and/or depression, and (2) examining how interpersonal styles relate to the comorbidity and chronicity of anxiety and depression.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Participants (
                      <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>
                       = 1800) were drawn from the 9‐year follow‐up of the
                      <jats:italic>Netherlands Study of Depression and Anxiety</jats:italic>
                      . Diagnostic data from baseline until the 9‐year follow‐up were used to determine diagnoses and chronicity. General interpersonal distress and style were derived from the IIP using the Structural Summary Method. Participants were grouped into four interpersonal style subtypes corresponding to the quadrants of the interpersonal circumplex.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Currently diagnosed participants reported higher general interpersonal distress and a more submissive style than those with past and no lifetime anxiety/depression. As predicted, a cold‐submissive style was associated with greater comorbidity and chronicity, also after adjusting for demographics.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study extends prior research on how patients' interpersonal style relates to psychopathology by using longitudinal, transdiagnostic data of individuals across different symptomatic stages. Our findings indicate that a cold‐submissive style is relatively common in more comorbid and chronic anxiety and depressive disorders. This highlights the clinical value of integrating interpersonal assessment into treatment planning.</jats:p>

text: {"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,21]],"date-time":"2026-09-21T05:01:53Z","timestamp":1789966913148,"version":"4.0.1"},"reference-count":67,"publisher":"Enviro Research Publishers","issue":"21","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,10]],"date-time":"2026-09-10T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1788998400000},"content-version":"unspecified","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http:\/\/creativecommons.org\/licenses\/by\/4.0\/"}],"content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"short-container-title":["Curr World Environ 2026"],"published-print":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,11]]},"abstract":"<jats:p>Abstract Biodiversity hotspots possess large numbers of endemic species in landscapes already threatened by extreme habitat loss. This review highlights how climate change is altering vulnerability, adaptation, resilience and species-loss risk across selected global hotspots, and suggests conservation responses that can reduce risk under present scenario of global warming.A narrative review was undertaken using peer-reviewed articles, major assessment reports and conservation-agency documents published mainly between 2000 and 2026, with emphasis on post-2015 literature. Selection of sources was on the basis of the following key themes: relevance to hotspot criteria, climate exposure, endemic-species vulnerability, climate refugia, ecological connectivity, regional case evidence and policy responses. The case studies were selectively chosen to exemplify tropical forests, islands, temperate and Mediterranean systems, semi-arid woodlands, coastal and marine interfaces, and heavily transformed mountain and river-basin landscapes. The analysis shows that hotspot vulnerability is highest where restricted-range endemism, habitat fragmentation, strong climatic exposure and limited adaptive capacity coincide. Endemic plants, amphibians, reptiles, island species, corals and other habitat specialists are especially sensitive because they often combine narrow ecological niches with low dispersal potential. Across the Amazon and Guianas, Amur-Heilong, Coastal East Africa, Madagascar, the Mediterranean Basin, Miombo woodlands, Southwest Australia, the Yangtze Basin and Indian hotspots, climate change intensifies existing threats by shifting climatic envelopes, increasing drought and fire, altering trophic interactions, increasing disease and invasion risk, and reducing the reliability of ecosystem services. Climate refugia, ecological corridors, restoration and community-based management emerge as recurring resilience mechanisms.Protecting biodiversity hotspots under climate change requires climate-smart protected-area design, landscape and seascape connectivity, fine-scale refugia protection, rapid greenhouse-gas mitigation, ecosystem restoration, ex situ safeguards for highly restricted species, and equitable governance involving local and Indigenous communities. The value of the hotspot framework therefore lies not only in identifying irreplaceable biodiversity, but also in guiding integrated adaptation and conservation action in a rapidly changing world.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.12944\/cwe.21.2.3","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,21]],"date-time":"2026-09-21T04:14:17Z","timestamp":1789964057000},"page":"467","update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.12944\/cwe.21","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Climate Change and Biodiversity Hotspots: Patterns of  Adaptation, Resilience, and Species Loss"],"prefix":"10.12944","volume":"2","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0009-0006-3665-7604","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Jyoti","family":"Arora","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"1 Department of Zoology, Miranda House, University of Delhi, Delhi, India"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"5089","published-online":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,10]]},"reference":[{"key":"ref0","doi-asserted-by":"crossref","unstructured":"Myers N., Mittermeier R.A., Mittermeier C.G., da Fonseca G.A.B., Kent J. It advances research on organizational climate risk perception by integrating perspectives on embeddedness and resource configurations. Based on 41 semi\u2010structured interviews with representatives of 22 logistics companies in the Osnabr\u00fcck region, we find that firms' resource configurations shape their capacity to perceive climate risks: Resource\u2010rich firms are more adept due to human resource slack, allowing them to process and document climate\u2010related sensory experiences and undertake anticipatory exercises. In contrast, resource\u2010poor firms display unrealistic optimism, leading to inadequate preparedness. While territorial embeddedness can broaden experience with climate impacts, embeddedness in interorganizational networks provides limited support for climate risk perception. The methodology integrates precipitation and temperature using the multi-lag approach. An initial pool of fifteen machine learning models were evaluated, and top-performing models were selected for further refinement through iterative ensemble stacking and weak learner elimination. Historical analysis (1983\u20132014) utilized CHIRPS and CHIRTS datasets. Future projections employed twelve bias-adjusted CMIP6 models and their ensemble mean (EnsMean) under SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5 for the near (2036\u20132067) and far (2068\u20132099) futures. Results showed notable improvements in model accuracy and efficiency across layers, with R\u00b2 and NSE exceeding 0.6 for all inflow simulations and for selected energy simulations (Bagre, Nangbeto, and Taabo). Projections indicated warming up to 4.5\u00b0C and spatially heterogeneous precipitation changes across basins and scenarios, with SSP5-8.5 projecting the most pronounced shifts. Inflow reductions are projected to reach up to 24% at Buyo and 13% at Nangbeto, while hydropower output may decline by up to 19% at Nangbeto and 58% at Taabo in the future. Conversely, Manantali and Taabo are projected to experience inflow increases, and Bagre may see energy gains of up to 42% under SSP5-8.5. These findings highlight heightened vulnerability, as well as contrasting opportunities across the region, underscoring the urgent need for adaptive management strategies, such as enhancing hydropower system resilience, diversifying energy portfolios, and integrating renewable sources to mitigate climate risks. Hydropower managers and policymakers must prioritize proactive measures to ensure energy security and sustainable resource management amid changing climatic American Water Resour Assoc"],"published-print":{"date-parts":[[2026,10]]},"abstract":"<jats:title>ABSTRACT<\/jats:title>\n                  <jats:p>Changes in precipitation regimes associated with climate variability and climate change pose significant challenges to water resource management, agriculture, and land\u2010use planning, particularly in socioeconomically strategic regions such as the Piracicaba River Basin, Brazil. This study analyzed precipitation series from 1985 to 2022 using data from 159 regularly spaced grid points across the basin. Pettitt, Mann\u2013Kendall, and Sen non\u2010parametric tests were applied to both annual totals and annual maximum 24\u2009h rainfall. Significant trends were identified in 22 grid points for annual precipitation and in 19 points for annual maximum daily rainfall. Breakpoints were concentrated in the late 1990s and between 2009 and 2012. Annual totals exhibited consistent negative Sen slopes, indicating a cumulative reduction in precipitation. In contrast, extreme daily rainfall showed spatially heterogeneous and lower\u2010magnitude trends, with no evidence of widespread intensification. Declining trends were concentrated near the basin headwaters and the Cantareira Water Supply System, suggesting potential implications for regional water security. Notably, the detected changes preceded the 2013\u20132015 water crisis in S\u00e3o Paulo. These findings highlight the need for continuous monitoring and adaptive water management strategies under increasing climate text:
{"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,4]],"date-time":"2026-09-04T10:20:36Z","timestamp":1788517236471,"version":"build-2803163510"},"reference-count":76,"publisher":"Wiley","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,4]],"date-time":"2026-09-04T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1788480000000},"content-version":"vor","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"},{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,4]],"date-time":"2026-09-04T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1788480000000},"content-version":"tdm","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http://doi.wiley.com/10.1002/tdm_license_1.1"}],"content-domain":{"domain":["bpspsychub.onlinelibrary.wiley.com"],"crossmark-restriction":true},"short-container-title":["Legal Criminol Psychol"],"abstract":"<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Purpose</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Evidence suggests that prisoners have more extensive victimization histories than non‐incarcerated people, which is linked to subsequent criminal behaviour. Additionally, violence and victimization are common in prisons and often underreported. Prior research has primarily focussed on the negative effects of victimization prior to incarceration. Thus, this review will explore the impact of victimization in prison on post‐release outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>A systematic literature search was conducted on PsycINFO, Web of Science, Scopus and Social Science Premium databases. Any peer‐reviewed studies written in English were eligible for inclusion if they analysed the relationship between victimization exposure in prison on post‐release outcomes or recidivism. Methodological quality was assessed using CASP Checklists. Of the 322 unique studies identified, 18 studies were selected based on the inclusion criteria.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>High rates of direct and witnessed victimization were reported. The majority of the quantitative studies found significant relationships between prison victimization and recidivism or other post‐release outcomes. Stronger evidence suggests recidivism, substance use and mental health outcomes are correlated with prison victimization, while evidence for interpersonal relationships and employment outcomes is weaker. Qualitative studies supported these findings and drew associations between prison violence and poorer outcomes upon release.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The results of this study indicate that trauma experienced while incarcerated is associated with greater risk of reoffending or other poor outcomes. However, the studies were limited to primarily adult samples in the United States, with mostly male participants; future research should seek to examine these effects in other populations.</jats:p>

load transfer by tailoring mesoscale architecture, yet most design strategies optimize global stiffness or energy absorption and only indirectly affect force redistribution. Here we introduce a computational\u2013experimental framework to explicitly design load\u2010distributing metamaterials by minimizing the variance of reaction forces transmitted to a support interface. Starting from a 3D face\u2010centered cubic (FCC) beam lattice, we model deformation using a linear\u2010elastic Timoshenko beam formulation and perform discrete topology optimization via Monte Carlo simulated annealing, where individual struts are selectively activated or removed. We demonstrate both single\u2010objective optimization for a prescribed indenter position and a multi\u2010objective formulation that enforces robust performance across multiple loading locations. Simulations show that optimized architectures transform highly localized support reactions into substantially more homogeneous force footprints, reducing the fraction of nearly unloaded nodes and capping peak forces. Stereolithography\u2010printed elastomeric lattices validate these predictions: quasi\u2010static pressure mapping reveals suppressed force hotspots and enlarged contact areas, while instrumented impact tests show earlier, more spatially distributed deformation and markedly improved repeatability\u2013especially for off\u2010center loading in multi\u2010objective designs. This work establishes load homogenization as a primary, quantifiable design target for architected materials, enabling protective interfaces and supports with tunable and robust title: Crossref record doi:10.3897/brics-econ.7.e185197: Stochastic Effects of Exchange Rate Fluctuations and Monetary-Fiscal Simulation on Exports in Asia
text:
{"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,3]],"date-time":"2026-09-03T15:12:48Z","timestamp":1788448368854,"version":"build-2803163510"},"reference-count":143,"publisher":"Pensoft Publishers","issue":"2","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,3]],"date-time":"2026-09-03T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1788393600000},"content-version":"vor","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/"}],"content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"short-container-title":["brics-econ"],"abstract":"<jats:p>The study explores the stochastic impacts of the exchange rate fluctuation and the synergistic effects of monetary-fiscal expansion simulations on export growth in Asia. It attempts to fill the gap between theoretical policy development and the practical uncertainty of policymakers in the emerging Asian markets.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The study is based on dual methodological approach. The study is based on a dual methodological approach. First, a Panel System Generalised Method of Moments (GMM) is used on a panel of Asian economies to identify structural determinants and interaction effects. Second, a Bayesian-estimated Medium-Scale version of the Dynamic Stochastic General Equation (DSGE) is employed to simulate the time-dependent reactions of exports to different policy and uncertainty shocks within twenty years span (the horizon taken to be twenty quarters). DSGE estimation was based on 26 years of historical data (January 1, 2000-December 31, 2025), and the impulse-response functions were simulated with horizon of twenty quarters (five years), which is compatible with canonical frequencies of business cycles taking into cognizance the transmission lags that accompany monetary and fiscal policy interventions required for the confirmation of the DSGE model convergence to the steady state. Besides, the homogeneity of monetary-fiscal policy regime that characterized the post-2000 era provides stability in the estimated deep parameters over the sample thus fulfilling the Lucas critique.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The GMM estimation shows that financial development and credit expansion are the most powerful structural forces of exports. Financial maturity only amplifies the advantages of competitive devaluations, according to the correlation between exchange rates and financial depth. The simulations in DSGE also show a coordinated expansion to be the most powerful stimulus as it will result in the greatest growth of exports of 0.934. A significant dampening in export growth is seen through policy uncertainty which is a big pull of exports in the economies of Asia. Conversely, the level of expansion of money supply, availability of domestic credit, financial development and consumption of energy has a positive impact on exports which in turn brings about the significance of liquidity, financial depth and production capacity in export expansion. The empirical evidence suggests that the competitiveness channel effect in the region of Asia is 0.867%. This gain is, nevertheless, dependent on financial maturity. In the case of the 16 poorest nations, the overall impact of monetary and fiscal expansion is expected to be positive if these economies are coupled with institutional reforms that reduce the cost of energy and debt. The simulated responses reveal stark structural asymmetries across the sample. While nominal exchange rate depreciation and co-ordinated monetary expansions represent extremely effective but necessarily short-lived export shocks - peaking invariably in Quarter four and reverting to the mean in Quarter twelve - the longer-run effects differ markedly. Bayesian inferences confirm that financial development is the only structural parameter that may lead to permanent (non-mean-reverting) export growth. By contrast, institutional weakness in forms of policy uncertainty, energy costs and black market labour exports inflicts significant negative asymmetries upon the fragile. The results show that the only way to avoid cyclical volatility is to prioritise holistic financial market development over short-term macroeconomic policymaking.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>The study provides a contribution to the literature by developing a methodological interface between the reduced-form empirical research and structural general-equilibrium modelling in the emerging Asian markets. It separates the structural processes to determine the causal transmission processes of monetary-fiscal synergy and exchange-rate volatility on export growth in a Bayesian DSGE model with diffuse priors adapted to the high-volatility regime typical in developing Asia. The model explicitly measures the sensitivity of the effectiveness of conventional policies that promote exports to policy uncertainty, as well as the fear of floating, which can be unduly precarious in linear panel regressions by including a stochastic volatility factor. The research establishes that the Asian poorest economies are constrained by structural asymmetries. The credibility intervals around the 90% high-posterior-density (HPD) intervals with prior means robustly confirm that, while these countries are equipped with highly elastic short-term absorption capacities to monetary and currency shocks, these economies are by nature incapable of permanently shifting their long-term economic paradigms via cyclical policies. Weak economies disproportionately suffer from policy uncertainty and supply-side restrictions, and are thus more likely to cancel out the effects of positive exchange rates.</jats:p>","DOI":"10.3897/brics-econ.7.e185197","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,3]],"date-time":"2026-09-03T14:14:57Z","timestamp":1788444897000},"page":"211-309","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Stochastic Four cases were selected where forecasts confidently predicted cold anomalies in Week 3: two associated with weakened stratospheric polar vortex (January 2013 and January 2010) and two occurring during active Madden\u2013Julian Oscillation (MJO, February 2013 and February 2005). For each case, ensemble experiments were performed with either the zonal\u2010mean stratosphere or the tropical belt relaxed towards ERA5 reanalysis or towards climatology. Results show that the January 2013 cold spell was primarily stratosphere\u2010driven: nudging the stratosphere towards climatology removed the Week 3 cold anomaly and the negative North Atlantic Oscillation (NAO) signal. In contrast, the stronger January 2010 cold anomaly was reduced but persisted after removing the stratospheric signal, indicating an additional contribution from tropospheric processes. In the tropical cases, tropical nudging affected NAO but did not affect the cold anomalies, suggesting additional contributing mechanisms. While the February 2005 cold spell coincided with a negative NAO, a negative NAO was not predicted for February 2013, highlighting the complexity of factors shaping European cold spells. To demonstrate feasibility of operational attribution, additional experiments were conducted with either the stratosphere nudged towards the ensemble member with the weakest predicted vortex or the tropics nudged towards the ensemble member with the strongest MJO. The results of these experiments are similar to those obtained with ERA5 (fifth generation of ECMWF atmospheric reanalyses of the global climate) nudging. Such experiments can serve as a counterpart to the climatological nudging when observations are unavailable, providing an opportunity to attribute predicted signals in operational forecasting. Overall, the results demonstrate that cold spells can arise through different dynamical pathways, potentially entailing different uncertainty. Targeted nudging experiments provide a practical attribution framework to assess the origin and confidence of subseasonal signals, linking physical attribution with operational In an online experiment, U.S. adults used ChatGPT to evaluate climate-related claims. We first conducted computational text analysis of GPT conversation logs, assessing valence, formality, bias, recency, authority cues, and semantic richness of ChatGPT\u2019s responses using language-model based classifiers and link-level metadata. Concurrently, we measured credibility judgments for both the claims and ChatGPT\u2019s responses through participant self-reports. Credibility perceptions were driven primarily by individual differences; greater acceptance of the scientific consensus, attention to climate change, prior familiarity with ChatGPT, and younger age predicted higher perceived credibility. Once these factors were accounted for, authority cues were associated with slightly less extreme climate attitudes, while positive valence and semantic richness correlated positively with perceived credibility. He compiled a selection of these correspondences into a Latin text, entitled Arcana Naturae Detecta. Here, we report a rare second edition of Arcana Naturae Detecta (1722), which includes original inscriptions confirming its acquisition in 1746 for the Carmelite College of Liberal Arts of San Joaqu\u00edn in Mexico City. Using occurrence data and environmental predictors, we evaluated the climate vulnerability, niche similarity and conservation priorities of Isoberlinia doka Craib and Stapf and Isoberlinia tomentosa (Harms) Craib and Stapf in Benin. These open‐forest species play an important ecological and socioeconomic role for local communities by providing firewood, charcoal, timber and medicinal resources. We modelled the climatic suitability of the species using maximum entropy (MaxEnt) under current conditions and Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP) 1–2.6, SSP 2–4.5 and SSP 5–8.5 scenarios for the period 2041–2060. We quantified climate niche overlap using Schoener's D and Hellinger's I indices. Spatial prioritization integrated climatic suitability, edaphic conditions, topographic moisture and anthropogenic pressure. Despite exhibiting high niche overlap ( D  = 0.635; I  = 0.788), the species responded differently. I. doka experienced severe habitat contraction, with losses of 62%–87% in the Sudanian zone (SZ) and Sudanian–Guinean zone (SGZ) and near‐complete loss of suitable habitat in the Guinean zone. I. tomentosa experienced more moderate losses (8%–12%) in the SZ and localized gains (6%–8%) in the SGZ. Priority areas were primarily located in the SZ, with less than 13% overlapping with existing protected areas. These findings demonstrate that niche conservatism does not imply equivalent climate vulnerability among closely related species. Therefore, conservation planning should be species‐specific and extend beyond protected areas through habitat restoration, agroforestry and targeted protection of priority populations. Such strategies support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals 13 and 15 by promoting climate change adaptation, biodiversity conservation, sustainable ecosystem management and local livelihoods. title: Crossref record doi:10.11591/ijeecs.v43.i3.pp965-974: Zero-trust IoT security using homomorphic encryption, blockchain, and machine learning
text: {"status":"ok","message-type":"work","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"indexed":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,11]],"date-time":"2026-09-11T18:06:04Z","timestamp":1789149964647,"version":"build-2803163510"},"reference-count":0,"publisher":"Institute of Advanced Engineering and Science","issue":"3","license":[{"start":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,1]],"date-time":"2026-09-01T00:00:00Z","timestamp":1788220800000},"content-version":"unspecified","delay-in-days":0,"URL":"http:\/\/creativecommons.org\/licenses\/by\/4.0\/"}],"content-domain":{"domain":[],"crossmark-restriction":false},"short-container-title":["IJEECS"],"abstract":"<jats:p>The growing deployment of internet of things (IoT) devices across healthcare, manufacturing, and smart infrastructure has introduced serious security vulnerabilities that can no longer be ignored. Traditional perimeter-based security models have proven inadequate for decentralized IoT environments, especially given that approximately 67% of these devices lack sufficient protection. To address this critical gap, this paper presents a unified security framework that brings together zero trust architecture (ZTA), homomorphic encryption (HE), blockchain, and machine learning (ML) into a single adaptive architecture. At its core, the framework employs Cheon-Kim-Kim-Song (CKKS) based HE for privacy-preserving computation, hyperledger fabric for decentralized identity and key management, and long short-term memory (LSTM) networks for real-time anomaly detection\u2014all operating directly on encrypted data. We validated our approach through extensive experiments on 150,000 samples across 50 IoT devices, and the results were impressive. The framework achieved 97.2% threat detection accuracy with an average response latency of just 120 ms, along with 97.2% resistance to penetration attacks. Notably, it also reduced energy consumption by 25% compared to conventional LSTM implementations. What makes these findings particularly significant is that our framework outperformed both ZTA-only and blockchain-only baselines\u2014by 5.7% and 8.9%, respectively\u2014while maintaining complete data privacy. Furthermore, scalability analyses confirmed linear scaling to over 1,000 devices across 20 edge nodes.                   <jats:p>Teacher well‐being in challenging educational contexts has important implications for sustainable professional learning, yet less is known about how job demands and job resources operate among EFL teachers in underexamined regional settings. Drawing on Job Demands‐Resources theory, this mixed‐methods study examined the direct and indirect relationships among job demands, job resources, resilience, teacher efficacy, work engagement and emotional exhaustion among EFL teachers in Western China. A total of 256 valid survey responses were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling, followed by semi‐structured interviews with eight teachers to interpret the quantitative patterns. The results showed that job demands significantly predicted emotional exhaustion, but not work engagement. Job resources showed no significant direct effects on either outcome. Instead, both resilience and teacher efficacy mediated the relationships between job demands, job resources and work engagement, whereas only resilience mediated the relationships between job demands, job resources and emotional exhaustion. The interview data further indicated that job demands were experienced as a clear source of fatigue but not necessarily as a reason to disengage from teaching, while resources became effective mainly when they were usable, timely, and connected to concrete problems of practice. The study extends JD‐R research by showing how demands and resources helped explain teacher well‐being in a challenging EFL context and demonstrating that teacher well‐being is closely tied to the conditions under which professional learning can be sustained.</jats:p>","DOI":"10.1111/ejed.70852","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,2]],"date-time":"2026-09-02T05:59:55Z","timestamp":1788328795000},"update-policy":"https://doi.org/10.1002/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["The Interplay of Job Demands, Job Resources and Personal Resources Among

                  <jats:p>Although artificial intelligence (AI) has become an integral component of language education, research has primarily emphasized technological factors influencing learning outcomes, with limited attention to the psychological attributes that enable students to benefit from AI‐supported instruction. Addressing this gap, the present study investigated whether EFL students' character strengths predict academic performance, resilience and psychological well‐being in AI‐integrated educational environments. A quantitative cross‐sectional design was employed with 773 undergraduate EFL students from Chinese universities. Participants completed validated measures of character strengths, resilience, psychological well‐being and academic performance. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and structural equation modelling (SEM). The findings demonstrated that character strengths were positively associated with all three outcomes. SEM further revealed that character strengths significantly predicted academic performance, resilience and psychological well‐being, accounting for substantial variance in each construct. These findings highlight character strengths as key psychological resources that support both academic achievement and psychological adaptation in AI‐supported language learning. The study extends current research by integrating positive psychology with AI‐enhanced education and underscores the importance of fostering students' psychological strengths alongside technological innovation.</jats:p>","DOI":"10.1111/ejed.70845","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,9,2]],"date-time":"2026-09-02T06:11:16Z","timestamp":1788329476000},"update-policy":"https://doi.org/10.1002/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Predicting EFL Students' Academic Performance, Resilience or Psychological Well‐Being From Their Character Strengths in

International policy learning and transfer are central to government approaches in these sectors. However, policies often show limited effectiveness when applied in varied contexts, likely due to assumptions of population homogeneity and over-reliance on socio-demographic characteristics. Using Multilevel Latent Class Analyses (MLCA) on over 17,000 respondents across 61 regions in nine OECD countries, we found that less sustainable behavioural patterns were prevalent across the three sectors, though with notable heterogeneity in the energy sector, and that socio-demographic characteristics failed to predict segment membership consistently. Individuals engaging in sustainable behaviours in one sector were more likely to do so in others, and unsustainable behaviours had similar positive associations across sectors, suggesting coordinated cross-sector interventions are crucial. Regional distribution of population segments was typically grouped geographically by country, underscoring the importance of contextual influences. However, we identified significant within-country variations in regional distributions, with some regions showing substantially different proportions of people in sustainable segments than neighbouring regions under identical national policies, highlighting the importance of regional context. Moving beyond traditional ad-hoc policy transfer approaches, we proposed a systematic framework for identifying evidence-based transfer opportunities, showing policymakers not only who needs interventions but where successful patterns emerge and which contexts may enable sustainable behaviours. These findings provide actionable insights for the international policy community seeking to accelerate behavioural change at the scale and speed required for climate mitigation.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1371\/journal.pclm.0001039","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,8,31]],"date-time":"2026-08-31T17:26:37Z","timestamp":1788197197000},"page":"e0001039","update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1371\/journal.pclm.corrections_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["From segmentation to strategy: Identifying population segments and regional patterns of environmental behaviour"],"prefix":"10.1371","volume":"5","author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0002-9327-6473","authenticated-orcid":true,"given":"Guanyu","family":"Yang","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"Amy","family":"Rodger","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0001-8197-3282","authenticated-orcid":true,"given":"Elif Naz","family":"\u00c7oker","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]},{"given":"David","family":"Shipworth","sequence":"additional","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"member":"340","published-online":{"date-parts":[[2026,8,31]]},"reference":[{"key":"pclm.0001039.ref001","volume-title":"Climate change 2023: synthesis report","author":"IPCC","year":"2023"},{"key":"pclm.0001039.ref002","doi-asserted-by":"crossref","first-page":"102969","DOI":"10.1016\/j.gloenvcha.2025.102969","article-title":"Addressing climate inaction as our greatest threat to sustainable development","volume":"91","author":"S Mackay","year":"2025","journal-title":"Global Environmental Change"},{"key":"pclm.0001039.ref003","volume-title":"Emissions Gap Report 2024: No more hot air \u2026 please! The aim of this paper is to explore the morning bed\u2010bath as a culturally embedded ICU nursing practice and to interpret how bodily care, professional identity, organisational routines and relational attentiveness intersect within this everyday activity. Informed by critical medical anthropology and phenomenology, the study draws on participant observation, ethnographic fieldnotes, and interviews with intensive care staff. The interpretation draws primarily on Foucault's concept of discipline, complemented by Bourdieu's notion of habitus and embodied practice, and Douglas's work on purity and symbolic order. Three interrelated themes emerged, forming a \u2018triptych of care\u2019: a) proximity and synchronicity to the patients' needs and clinical condition, which revealed skilled bodily attentiveness, clinical judgement and nursing agency, alongside negotiations of professional knowledge, and authority; b) the creation of a zone of safety and privacy, where bodily exposure, dignity, relational care, and professional interaction were negotiated within the ICU environment; and c) the removal of dirt and impurities, which served immediate clinical and hygienic purposes while also carrying cultural and professional meanings associated with bodily presentation, cleanliness, and order. The findings suggest that the morning bed\u2010bath in the ICU studied was not merely a technical nursing task, but a culturally embedded and routinised practice through which temporal and organisational routines, embodied care, symbolic order, and professional nursing values are                   <jats:p>
                    Soil organic carbon (SOC) plays a critical role in climate regulation, particularly in agroecosystems where soil management practices significantly influence carbon sequestration. In the Mediterranean Basin, olive groves represent a major agricultural system whose carbon storage potential remains insufficiently characterized at large spatial scales. This study assessed SOC stocks and their saturation status in 52 olive orchards sampled across five Mediterranean countries (Spain, Greece, Italy, Portugal, and Morocco), with 39 orchards retained for stock calculations after quality control of bulk density and coarse fragment data. SOC was quantified by both dry combustion and the Nelson and Sommers wet oxidation method. Agreement between methods was formally tested, and a carbonate‐dependent positive bias of the dry combustion method (
                    <jats:italic>r</jats:italic>
                     = +0.20 between ISO−NS difference and carbonate content,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     < 0.0001) led us to retain Nelson & Sommers values for all stock calculations. Bulk density measured with Kopecky cylinders was retained over a Saxton & Rawls pedotransfer estimate after a paired comparison showed poor concordance (Lin's CCC = 0.08; 95% LoA = ±0.5 g cm
                    <jats:sup>−3</jats:sup>
                    ). The maximum SOC saturation limit (SOC_max) was estimated from the silt + clay protective fraction, with consistent (1−FG) coarse‐fragment correction applied to both current and maximum stocks so that the saturation deficit (SOC_potential = SOC_max−SOC_current) is a directly comparable, physically meaningful gap. Multivariate analyses (PCA, LDA with Wilks' Λ, two‐way PERMANOVA) revealed that olive orchards are organized along a single dominant intensification gradient (PC1, 30.5% of variance; CD1, 91.7% of canonical variance,
                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                     < 0.001) rather than into separable agronomic management classes; the gradient is robust to the exclusion of operationally tautological variables. Mediterranean olive groves operated on average at 41% of their textural carbon‐storage capacity, with a mean saturation deficit of 64 Mg C ha
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    (59% of SOC_max). The deficit varied along the intensification axis in the direction predicted by carbon‐saturation theory (saturation level: 49% organic, 39% conventional, 33% high‐density), although per‐group differences did not reach significance with
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                     = 9–12 orchards per management class. Super‐intensive (hedgerow) systems with > 1000 trees ha
                    <jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>
                    were not represented in the sample, and this is acknowledged as a limitation. These findings highlight that intensification, more than the organic‐versus‐conventional dichotomy, structures the multivariate variability of Mediterranean olive groves, and that current SOC stocks lie well below textural saturation in most systems, indicating substantial potential for additional carbon sequestration through soil‐conservation practices.

These fluctuations are often viewed as the consequence of random variations in the local hydraulic conditions and sediment movement. While such explanations emphasize small\u2010scale processes, they do not account for how larger\u2010scale channel structure may organize these fluctuations. The role of reach\u2010scale channel morphology in controlling sediment transport remains unexplored. Here we show that the temporal variability of sediment transport results from switching\u00a0between a finite set of recurrent morphological configurations. We used the results of a former long\u2010term (1200\u2010hr) laboratory experiment conducted under constant water discharge and sediment supply, in\u00a0which 16 morphological states were identified using image processing. The present paper shows that the temporal evolution of these states can be modeled using a discrete\u2010time Markov process. We assume that sediment transport depends on the active state of the channel. The state\u2010dependent transport rates can be simulated using either an empirical probability distribution fitted to the data or a Gamma distribution with parameters dependent on stream power. We introduced a third model that ignores morphological state, and simulates transport rates using the bootstrap technique. We used the three models to generate long time series of transport rates, the ensemble statistics of which were compared with the experimental statistics. The three models perform equally well for predicting the mean transport rate and its variance, but the purely Markovian model is superior for predicting the temporal features of transport rates. These findings indicate that variability in bedload transport rates mainly results from the persistence and succession of a finite set of morphological states.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.1029\/2026wr044293","type":"journal-article","created":{"date-parts":[[2026,8,29]],"date-time":"2026-08-29T09:37:55Z","timestamp":1787996275000},"update-policy":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1002\/crossmark_policy","source":"Crossref","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["Morphological Here, we analyse the role of earthquake\u2010induced rock mass damage over late Pleistocene to Holocene time scales, as a conditioning factor for modern landslides, using distinct element numerical modelling to assess spatial and temporal patterns of fracture propagation influenced by varying glacier thickness. Conceptualised numerical models were parameterised by in\u00a0situ rock mass, glacial and topographic conditions in Serpentine valley, located in Prince William Sound, Alaska, where several large landslides are actively developing along the western valley wall. Results show that although rigid glacier buttressing reduces co\u2010seismic rock mass damage, it does not suppress it completely, and damage occurs both above and below the glacier surface elevation. We demonstrate that topography, and especially steep slopes with topographic convexity, as well as preexisting damage of joint networks and faults inherited from tectonic and exhumation induced stresses, exert primary control on the location of new co\u2010seismic damage. Simulations representing a simplified deglaciation sequence over the past 25\u2009ka, with a series of 10 evenly spaced earthquakes, generated rock mass damage patterns that qualitatively match in\u00a0situ landslide structural and kinematic observations at one instability in Serpentine valley. Our conceptual study helps clarify the role of repeated seismicity over glacial timescales as a long\u2010term conditioning process for paraglacial rock slope failure, highlighting spatial and temporal patterns of progressive damage accumulation, with outcomes relevant for modern landslide hazard In many cases, their interpretation has often proved contentious; as a result, the non\u2010generic term discrete debris accumulations (DDA) has been used to describe them and, over the last 50 years, some have been interpreted as fossil rock glaciers of late Quaternary age. However, detailed accounts of their sedimentology and structural assessments of surrounding rock slopes have been lacking, despite the insights into processes that such investigations would allow. Here, and for the first time in the British Isles, we use detailed lithological and structural modelling and analyses to investigate a well\u2010defined DDA in the Nantlle Valley of North Wales. We show that component clasts within the landform are from rockfall debris originally detached from upslope rockwalls above by relatively small\u2010scale failure events. The results of 2D rockfall analysis demonstrate that a significant proportion of component debris could not have been deposited directly from rockfall. Instead, we conclude that the DDA was formed by downslope remobilisation of thick talus deposits, and movement was associated with strong compressional flow in the frontal margin. We argue that the only plausible mechanism that could have been responsible was the internal creep of ground ice that had developed within the talus. As a result, we argue that the DDA is a fossil rock glacier. Its formation in western Britain with former high levels of precipitation calls into question some of the palaeoenvironmental implications often applied to such                   <jats:p>
                    With advances in global and regional circulation models, the high‐resolution simulation of atmospheric variables has become increasingly feasible. In this study, we use IsoRSM, an isotope‐enabled regional spectral model, to improve the simulation of precipitation and its isotopic composition over tropical Costa Rica, which is marked by a pronounced topography and is surrounded by two oceans. A 14‐year (2010–2023) simulation was performed at a relatively high spatial (5 km) and temporal (6‐hourly) resolution over a 6° × 6° domain covering Costa Rica and surrounding regions. Model outputs were evaluated using observations from 58 precipitation‐amount sites and 27 isotope‐monitoring sites and were compared with a 10 km IsoRSM simulation from a previous study over a larger spatial domain. After applying quantile mapping (QM) bias correction, the model generally captured the spatial patterns and seasonal cycles of precipitation inputs and precipitation isotopes across Costa Rica. The mean Kling‐Gupta efficiency (KGE) for bias‐corrected precipitation δ
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    H reached 0.43, and the 5 km simulation outperformed the previous 10 km run, highlighting the benefits of improved topographic representation. IsoRSM also clearly simulated the δ
                    <jats:sup>2</jats:sup>
                    H‐δ
                    <jats:sup>18</jats:sup>
                    O relationship and the interannual variability along the topographical gradient of Costa Rica. Thus, the bias‐corrected IsoRSM outputs offer a promising source of simulated data for further application, such as the forcing data for isotope‐enabled eco‐hydrological models.

The self\u2010synchronization transmission motion of two motors can achieve the screening requirement and save electrical energy by driving one single inductor motor. Nevertheless, this technology is currently only applicable to the condition of two motors. The self\u2010synchronization transmission of multiple motors (more than 2) can't be applied in industry. To solve this problem, the theory of the composite synchronization transmission is proposed and the energy transfer mechanism is investigated on a nonlinear coupled vibrating system with three eccentric rotors (ERs) driven by inductor motors. The mathematical model of the coupled system is first established. Then the synchronization conditions and stability criteria are given through the Routh\u2010Hurwitz stability criterion. The method of radial basis function\u2010neural network adaptive sliding model (RBF\u2010NNASMC) is introduced in the self\u2010synchronization transmission to realize the composite synchronization transmission. In addition, the controller is designed combined with the dynamical model. The stability of the controlling system is proved by the Lyapunov stability theory. Finaly, numerical results are given to illustrate the consistency with the theory and the effectiveness of the control method. The results indicate that the theory of composite synchronization transmission can realize the energy transfer by the vibrating system so as to save the electric energy.                   <jats:p>
                    Self‐regulation (SR) plays a central role in instructed language learning, as it enables learners to set goals, monitor progress, and adapt learning behaviour through reflection. We investigate the contribution of two core self‐regulatory processes—performance control (PC) and reflection (R)—to attainment (A) in structure‐focused L2 English and L2 German courses. In the context of our study, these courses are taught to language majors and involve explicit, analytically oriented instruction in language structure, including phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics, rather than skills‐focused language teaching. Addressing calls to move beyond self‐report measures, we drew on behavioural indicators of self‐regulation, including engagement in non‐graded Moodle activities and participation in structured reflection tasks. Data was collected longitudinally at four time points over one academic year from 119 learners enrolled in English L2/German L3 (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                    = 70) and German L2/English L3 (
                    <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
                    = 49) programmes. Relationships among PC, R, and A were examined using longitudinal linear mixed‐effects models consistent with cyclical accounts of self‐regulated learning. Analyses supported a process‐consistent pattern in which R was associated with PC, while PC predicted A and R showed no direct association with A once PC was included in the model. Importantly, these relationships differed across L2 learning contexts, with PC showing a stronger association with A in L2 German than L2 English. The findings point to the value of linking structured reflection with behavioural engagement in low‐stakes practice, particularly in the L2 German context, rather than treating reflection as an isolated instructional target.

maintaining the delivery of essential services to our society, including power generation, water supply, transport and telecommunication. Computational modelling has become integral to infrastructure planning and management, enabling the exploration of system interdependencies and the testing of adaptation strategies against unprecedented conditions. However, infrastructure model outputs are conditional on a range of uncertain assumptions about the system drivers and properties, both in the present day and in the future under climate change. In this article, we show how global sensitivity analysis can be used to consistently quantify and attribute the uncertainty in infrastructure model outputs as a consequence of input uncertainties, using two examples from the energy and water sector in the United Kingdom (UK). We find that dominant uncertainties vary case by case, as does the relative importance of climate uncertainty. We argue that structured uncertainty and sensitivity analysis should be incorporated more consistently across infrastructure modelling sectors to support resilient infrastructure Here, we analyze the temperature and precipitation thresholds of limiting gross primary productivity (GPP) of tundra ecosystems in the Arctic and TP from 1982 to 2100, using a combination of observational data sets and simulations. We found that the temperature thresholds limiting GPP increase in both regions have steadily increased since 1982 and are projected to continue rising. In contrast, precipitation thresholds show significant upward trends in the Arctic but considerable temporal variability in the TP. By 2100, precipitation limitation of GPP is projected to exert a stronger influence in browning zones than in greening zones, whereas temperature limitation is more pronounced in greening zones. Our results reveal the diverse vegetation responses to temperature and precipitation in the Arctic and TP                     Climate factors such as temperature and rainfall influence vector-borne disease dynamics. Consequently, climate change is affecting the global distribution of diseases such as dengue. Natural climate variability (NCV), which adds noise to the climate signal, alters the future climate trajectory, but is rarely analysed in climate-health analyses. In this study, extending a published model of climate suitability for
                    <jats:italic>Ae. aegypti</jats:italic>
                    , we consider a climate-sensitive dengue transmission model. Using 100 climate projections up to 2100 from the Community Earth System Model (a climate model including climate change and NCV), each run under the same shared socioeconomic pathway scenario, we generate 100 equally plausible simulations of the future basic reproduction number of dengue globally and the population at risk. We quantify the difference in transmission suitability between the most-suitable and least-suitable projections (i.e., uncertainty due to NCV) and demonstrate that NCV affects future suitability for transmission, dominating epidemiological parameter uncertainty in many locations. While the global population at risk from dengue (and, as we show, other vector-borne diseases) is expected to increase, NCV affects its precise value. Our findings demonstrate that NCV should be routinely incorporated into climate-sensitive epidemiological projections, and a key output of our research is the provision of a methodological framework for this. Accounting for NCV will enable public health policy decisions to be informed by the range of possible future outcomes.
